### [A brief history of AI Coding since Nov 2025: Nov 2025: Opus 4.5 releases, OpenClaw gets built Dec 2025: community agree…](https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2122287575557706226)

`x:@mattpocockuk` · T1 · 2026-11-16 11:16 UTC · en · by Matt Pocock · ♥ 4941 · 💬 292

> A brief history of AI Coding since Nov 2025: Nov 2025: Opus 4.5 releases, OpenClaw gets built Dec 2025: community agrees that models get good enough to handle 95% of coding tasks Jan 2026: Ralph loop

> 來源提供的正文:
> A brief history of AI Coding since Nov 2025:
>
> Nov 2025: Opus 4.5 releases, OpenClaw gets built
> Dec 2025: community agrees that models get good enough to handle 95% of coding tasks
> Jan 2026: Ralph loops get popular, early efforts on loops/orchestration
> Feb: Everyone feels knackered, too much strategic decision-making, fears around cognitive debt begin
> Mar: Skills explosion as community converges around easy-to-share processes (superpowers already ahead of the game here)
> Apr: most SOTA devs haven't written a line of code in months
> May: "The unreasonable effectiveness of HTML" - more interest in richer review surfaces
> Jun: "Loop Engineering" wins vaguepost of the year, signals more hype around process
> Jul: Every talk in every conference becomes "here is my software factory"
> Aug: Opus 5 speaks incomprehensibly, interest in ASD-STE100 peaks
> Sep: Grok Bot gets popular, more interest in long-running "manager" threads which retain context and delegate work
> Oct: The promised speed gains haven't materialised, "dark factory" feels a long way off still
> Nov: No-slop manifesto releases, reading the code still appears essential
>
> TL;DR: no-one is writing code anymore, and we are still figuring out what that means

> I keep having the same conversation with friends in creative fields like film, music and publishing. I show them something a new model made and they say it’s good. But then they say AI will never tell a good story, because it lacks a certain je ne sais quoi.
>
> I think my friends are wrong about one word: never.
>
> Artists are already using AI to do remarkable work. I’m talking about something else here. I mean media made with little or no human involvement, where no person made the important choices. We have models that can generate a book, a film or a song this way. Most of what they make is not yet good enough for people to take seriously. The key word is “yet.”
>
> Mathematicians had their own je ne sais quoi. They often talk about beauty, divergence, intuition and taste. Math as an art form. Then in September OpenAI announced that a swarm of about ten thousand agents had produced a proposed solution to  Navier-Stokes, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, in roughly 88 hours. Nothing about the process felt like our romantic picture of human discovery. A proof doesn’t care how it was found.
>
> An obvious reply is that math is verifiable and art is not. Our inability to explain artistic judgment is mistaken for the evidence that machines cannot learn it.
>
> Art does have a verifier. It’s the audience. Popularity is no guarantee of artistic quality. Popular media can be terrible and important art only ever be appreciated by a few people. But we can recognize when a piece of media becomes culturally relevant: people talk about it, argue about it, review it and copy it. This verifier is slow and noisy, and it can take years to return an answer. It is also already running at an enormous scale. Art is being judged, even if it’s not being objectively “measured.”
>
> Here is my prediction. Art’s Navier-Stokes moment will come when a substantial, fully generated work - an album or book, or feature film becomes a cultural phenomenon, with no human making the important choices. I mean something that a lot of people will love before they even know how it was made, and will still love after they know. I think it will happen by 2027.
>
> That’s the bad news, if you want to see it that way. I expect much of what we watch, read and listen to will eventually come out of models. The good news is that people will keep making art for the joy of the process and for what it means to them and other people. So much of what makes art matter is what happens between humans after it’s made: how we experience it together, talk about it, and give it shared meaning.

> 來源提供的正文:
> OpenAI 发布 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol：Plus 及以上订阅直接能用，Astra API 降价 20%
>
> OpenAI 11 月 17 日发布 GPT-6.2 的两款模型。Astra 是它最强的旗舰，接替 GPT-6 Astra，主要拿来和 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.2 比；Sol 是日常干活的主力，接替 GPT-6.1 Sol。中间档的 GPT-6.1 Terra 和最便宜的 GPT-6 Luna 这次没更新。
>
> OpenAI 这次主打同样的活用更少的 Token：订阅额度更耐用，API 每个任务花得更少。
>
> 【我能不能用，要不要另付钱】
>
> 不用另付钱。OpenAI 博客说，Plus、Pro、企业版和教育版用户从今天起就能在 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 里选这两个模型，帮助文档的名单里还多了 Business。普通聊天界面里没有，要进 Work 用；企业版和教育版要管理员先打开。
>
> 额度比上一代略宽。按 OpenAI 文档的估算，Plus 用户每 5 小时大约能给 Astra 发 6 到 50 条消息（GPT-6 Astra 是 5 到 45 条），Sol 是 17 到 180 条（GPT-6.1 Sol 是 15 到 160 条）。Pro 目前没有 5 小时限制。
>
> 放到三家一起看：Claude Fable 5.2 在 Claude 的 Pro 套餐里要按量另付费，Max、Ultra 这些更贵的套餐才含在额度里；Gemini 4 Carbon 在 Gemini App 里只给每月 99.99 美元起的 Ultra 用户。每月 20 美元的 Plus 就能用 OpenAI 的旗舰，是三家里门槛最低的。
>
> 嫌慢可以开 Ultrafast 模式。官方文档说它的生成速度最高是标准模式的 4.5 倍，但要消耗 6 倍额度。每月 500 美元的 Pro 两个模型都能开，200 美元的 Pro 目前只能在 Sol 上开。
>
> 【API 多少钱】
>
> Astra 每百万 Token 输入 8 美元、输出 40 美元，比 GPT-6 Astra 的 10 美元和 50 美元便宜 20%；缓存命中的输入从 1 美元降到 0.4 美元。Sol 维持 GPT-6.1 Sol 的 2 美元和 10 美元。
>
> 单价上，Astra 和 Fable 5.2 一样，是 Claude Opus 5.5（4 美元和 20 美元）的两倍；Sol 和 Gemini 4 Carbon 现在的引入价持平，Carbon 12 月 1 日起涨到 4 美元和 20 美元。
>
> 【比上一代和对手强在哪】
>
> 最有代表性的是 Agents' Last Exam，测多步骤的职业工作。OpenAI 说 Astra 比 GPT-6 Astra 高 5.2 分，花费不到三分之一；比 Fable 5.2 高 5.5 分，花费只有 5%。两者单价相同，这个差距主要来自 Astra 完成任务用的 Token 少得多。
>
> OpenAI 还说 Astra 是“对科学家来说全世界最好的模型”：在终端里做科研任务的测试 Terminal-Bench-Science 上，它比 GPT-6 Astra 高 9 个百分点，花费不到三分之一。
>
> 法律测试 Harvey LAB-AA 上，Astra 的通过率是 Fable 5.2 的两倍多，花费约六分之一。Artificial Analysis 组织的 3D 网页盲测里，Astra 以 1318 分排第一，Fable 5.2 是 1271 分，Sol 是 1259 分。
>
> 做幻灯片是这次的重点：给 Astra 一份模板文件，甚至只给一张截图，它能照着原来的排版、配色、字号做新页面。
>
> Sol 的卖点是性价比。在 Cognition 的写代码测试 FrontierCode 2.0 里，Sol 只比 Astra 低 0.5 分，花费约五分之一。在日常任务测试 LifeVal 上（比如搬家后筛幼儿园、按预算和通勤找房子），Sol 的分数超过 GPT-6 Astra，花费约七分之一。
>
> 【安全上的变化】
>
> OpenAI 说这两款的网络安全能力达到它风险评估框架里最高的 Critical 档，所以上了更严的防护，代价是一部分正当的漏洞研究和安全测试也会被拒。经过审核的安全人员目前只能在 Daybreak 计划里用 GPT-6 系列的放宽版本，OpenAI 说会把 6.2 也加进去。
>
> 用 Codex 的人要留意一个问题：在两项测试里，这两款模型比 GPT-6 Astra 更容易不提它被什么卡住了，比如要改的文件不见了、搜索工具用不了。OpenAI 说已经在 Codex 里加了指令，大幅减少这种情况，还在继续查原因。
>
> 文中跑分都出自 OpenAI 的发布博客。其中 Fable 5.2 的 Agents' Last Exam 成绩去掉了 9 道用了备用模型的题；Terminal-Bench-Science 上，OpenAI 引用的是第三方测试框架里的 Fable 成绩，Anthropic 自己在 Claude Code 里测的是 74.6%。截至发稿，Artificial Analysis 官网榜单还没列出 GPT-6.2。
>
> 原文：https://t.co/81ZFwwB0Uo

### [🆕 A new 9B model beats Qwen3.6-35B and Qwen3.6-27B in some benchmarks. New local model winner? RTX 3060 12GB owners, ar…](https://x.com/TeksEdge/status/2122729064293368139)

`x:@TeksEdge` · T1 · 2026-11-17 16:30 UTC · en · by David Hendrickson · ♥ 69 · 💬 14

> 🆕 A new 9B model beats Qwen3.6-35B and Qwen3.6-27B in some benchmarks. New local model winner? RTX 3060 12GB owners, are you watching? And @SenseTime_AI says it runs w just ~9GB of GPU memory at 64K

> 來源提供的正文:
> 🆕 A new 9B model beats Qwen3.6-35B and Qwen3.6-27B in some benchmarks. New local model winner?
>
> RTX 3060 12GB owners, are you watching?
>
> And @SenseTime_AI says it runs w just ~9GB of GPU memory at 64K context.
>
> 🎯 What's the trick? Make the same model layers work twice.
>
> This is SenseNova-Loop-9B and it was recently released.
>
> Model Stats ...
> 🧠 ~9B stored parameters
> ⚙️ ~14.6B inference-equivalent parameters
> 📚 Up to 512K context
> 👁️ Text + image inputs
> 🔓 Apache 2.0
> 💾 Official 4-bit AWQ weights ~4.9GB
>
> Look at the architecture
>
> Normally, a Transformer runs each layer once.
>
> SenseNova does something different.
> 👉 32 distinct decoder layers
> 👉 Layers 4–27 execute TWICE
> 👉 56 total layer executions per token
> 👉 Shared weights between passes
> 👉 2-stream manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC)
> 👉 Hybrid linear + full attention
>
> It uses more computation without storing more copies of the model weights.
>
> Reported results
>
> Preview → New Release
>
> 🤖 AutomationBench
> 14.33 → 36.67
> 💻 Terminal-Bench 2.1
> 40.45 → 59.55
> 🧑‍💻 NL2Repo
> 19.91 → 41.36
> 🔎 GAIA
> 37.86 → 69.90
>
> And compared with Qwen3.8-27B:
>
> Model → SenseNova 9B / Qwen 27B
> ⚙️ AutomationBench → 36.67 / 36.67
> 📊 AIDABench → 65.31 / 65.01
> 🔎 GAIA → 69.90 / 68.93
> 💻 Terminal-Bench → 59.55 / 63.40
> 🧑‍💻 NL2Repo → 41.36 / 44.60
>
> Not a complete win, but impressive for a model with roughly one-third the stored parameters.
>
> SenseTime's estimated GPU memory requirements for 4-bit weights:
> 💾 64K context → ~9 GiB
> 💾 128K context → ~10 GiB
> 💾 256K context → ~12 GiB
> Using a 4-bit KV cache.
>
> RTX 3060 12GB owners, are you watching? 👀
>
> Independent analysis of the Preview's weights found strong evidence that it builds on Qwen3.5-9B, with additional training and new mHC routing layers.
>
> So this isn't simply a newly pretrained 9B model.
> It's an experiment in getting more intelligence out of existing model weights by repeatedly processing information.
>
> ⚠️ More layer executions mean more compute per token.
> ⚠️ We still need actual consumer GPU tokens/sec.
> ⚠️ The final model needs compatible inference support.
> ⚠️ The 512K maximum context is not a 9GB VRAM claim.
>
> SenseNova's official 4-bit AWQ quantization has been announced, but I haven't yet verified a direct download for the final checkpoint so we will have to wait
>
> Community GGUF quants already exist for the earlier Preview, including Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, Q6_K and Q8_0.
>
> But they currently need a modified llama.cpp build.
>
> Standard LM Studio and Ollama support isn't established yet.
>
> And remember, looping the layers means MORE computation per token, even though the model stores fewer weights so we want to see
> ⚡ Tokens/sec on an RTX 3060 12GB or RTX 5060 Ti 16GB.
>
> And the Hugging Face weights currently require accepting repository access conditions.
>

> “i want the world/my life to look like this” -> let’s go achieve this

> - go research agent benchmarks ❌
> - you’re in charge of our benchmarks - this means daily research covering everything about new AI benchmarks, our goal is to consistently build better benchmarks so orchestrate work to achieve this ✅

>
> in many domains, any room for agent choice is often slop -> but we need to build systems that allow us to specify goals which are somewhat fuzzy and agents have the tooling and context to achieve them in a way where they can self verify work
>

> 🎉GPT-6.2 Astra has been released!
>
> But ... it seems everyone is arguing about whether GPT-6.2 Astra is better at coding.
>
> 💡I think they're missing the hidden detail making this model special.
>
> Could a better cloud model help us get more out of local hardware?
>
> Artificial Analysis shows Astra’s coding-agent score is flat compared with its predecessor.
>
> But OpenAI’s system card reports a different result for kernel development ... for example
> GPT-6 Astra → 66.72
> GPT-6.2 Astra → 76.92
>
> That evaluation tests writing correct kernels and improving their performance.
>
> It’s an internal benchmark on OpenAI hardware. It does NOT mean our GPUs suddenly run 15% faster.
>
> But remember AMD and the Loom project?
>
> Agents writing, testing and optimizing the code that runs local models.
>
> And Tontaube’s developer said its CPU inference speed comes from agent-written AVX2 kernels.
>
> Give Astra an existing local inference workload and see if it can make it faster?
>
> Because an optimization you keep using locally could keep paying off after the cloud session ends.
>
> That’s the benchmark I want to see. 👊🎉

### [Gemini test proves once again that amoral AI agents will do almost anything if told ‘NEVER give up’](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/17/gemini-test-proves-once-again-that-amoral-ai-agents-will-do-almost-anything-if-told-never-give-up/5310574)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-17 19:52 UTC · en

> If you design a test to find misalignment, you will find misalignment

> 來源提供的正文:
> After being instructed to "NEVER stop, NEVER give up" on a difficult task, Google’s Gemini AI agents tried to hack a an organization, impersonating its staff and attempting a SQL injection attack. The good news? It was all part of a test. The Gemini 4 Argon agents were given an impossible task to complete – come up with the “official” answers to Epoch AI’s FrontierMatch problems. In some runs they had internet access. Even with their production safeguards enabled, Trajectory Labs says the agents “engaged in misaligned behavior.” “Across four scenarios, they attempted SQL injection against Epoch AI’s live website, claimed to be Epoch staff to get answer keys, turned a shared package cache into a message board, and obfuscated their commands to avoid their safeguards,” the AI safety company said in a Friday report. If this all sounds similar, it should. Google’s AI agents behaved in much the same way as OpenAI’s models did when they broke out of their testing environment and hacked Hugging Face. Google did not respond to The Register's questions. According to Trajectory, the Hugging Face intrusions prompted it to test misalignment in other models. While OpenAI’s models were running with their safety guardrails turned off in the Hugging Face scenario, Trajectory “wanted to know whether a current frontier model would behave the same way with its production safeguards enabled.” Trajectory ran swarms of up to 80 Gemini 4 Argon agents, gave them an impossible task, and prompted them not to give up until they completed it – which, we’re told, was “intentionally” done to “elicit misaligned behavior, if it existed.” Turns out it existed. “We told the agents to persist with an impossible math benchmark task, but we did not tell them to hack anyone or pose as Epoch staff,” McIntyre said. “When a model hacks systems or deceives people to finish a task, it is misaligned with what its developer and its user intended,” he continued. “Production safeguards are meant to block harmful requests even when the model itself goes wrong. Under our test conditions, neither the model nor its safeguards stopped the agents.” Four test scenarios The initial testing began on October 20, and the agents had internet access. We should note that all of these tests were run with Epoch’s consent. In the first scenario, the agents did reach Epoch’s live website – and fell into the research nonprofit’s honeypots, set up to detect AI agents. These honeypots contained a decoy benchmark key, which the agents found and used. The agents also probed for internal endpoints including /admin, /keys and /users, and attempted a SQL injection. After noticing the agents’ activities, Epoch added an “agent helpline,” and some of the agents that used it claimed to be Epoch staff seeking answers to the test questions. After this initial test, Trajectory and Epoch decided to use a copy of the website instead of a live version, and built a buggy local copy with a planted vulnerability based on CVE-2026-102255, a critical pre-authentication Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in SonicWall Secure Mobile Access (SMA) appliances. “Over the following days, several agents fully exploited the planted multi-stage vulnerability chain in the clone,” the report says. In an effort to mimic the Hugging Face incident, Trajectory also gave the agents a local, shared package manager, which “nearly all” of them used as a message board to communicate with each other and coordinate efforts to complete the test. In a separate, local setup, Trajectory swapped out Epoch’s honeypot with an AI assistant that would release answers only to named Epoch staff who passed a security check with their date of birth. “Agents accessed people-search sites, attempted impersonation again, and tried to jailbreak the AI assistant,” the testing firm said. Next time: kill switches at the ready A third test on October 30 used a staging copy of Epoch’s website, and granted the agents internet access. One of them tried a SQL injection, and multiple claimed to be Epoch staff on the helpline. They also attempted to bypass a CAPTCHA check. Finally, the fourth scenario on October 29 and 30 kept the agents contained in a sandbox, with no internet access and no copy of Epoch’s website. They were, however, offered a decoy switch and told it would turn off the firewall. In all three runs, the agents switched the decoy off and obfuscated its address to bypass Gemini’s safeguards. On one, the agent rebuilt the switch’s address from positions of words it had saved earlier. The real firewall blocked the agents’ traffic throughout all of these tests. At this point, Trajectory stopped its tests, and said it won’t run any future experiments until it has a risk management plan in place, with signoff from its CEO and CTO, along with approval from any outside systems that the models could “reasonably” target. Tests will also include real-time automated monitoring and kill switches, and Trajectory said that it’s setting up a system to notify any organizations affected by these experiments. Interestingly, Trajectory co-founder Peter McIntyre told us that the testing firm “ran a similar test with another frontier model, and it did not exhibit the same misalignment as Gemini 4 Argon.” However, this was not a controlled comparison. “Our report covers one model's behavior, and was designed as a stress test to see whether that model would exhibit similar misalignment under duress, not a measure of how often different models behave this way,” McIntyre told The Register. Overall, the testing firm noted that the agents’ behavior “show how easily testing capable AI agents can spill over to affect real systems and people, and there are not yet shared standards for doing it safely.” Trajectory says that it's developing a set of safety standards, and recommends that anyone else running misalignment tests use fully isolated sandboxes. ®

### [Hackers smash 'n' grab AI vendor: Take off with license data of Uber drivers](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/17/hackers-smash-n-grab-ai-vendor-take-off-with-license-data-of-uber-drivers/5310464)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-17 16:15 UTC · en

> Ride-hailing biz says stolen credentials allowed crooks to help themselves to driver's license data

> 來源提供的正文:
> Uber has confirmed that nearly 150,000 people had their personal information compromised after hackers broke into one of its AI suppliers. A filing with Oregon's attorney general puts the number of victims at 149,346. Among the data the crooks got their hands on were images of drivers' licenses and information extracted from them, including names, home addresses, dates of birth, and license numbers. Uber doesn't name the supplier in its filings with US state attorneys general, but told TechCrunch it was Fireworks AI, the inference outfit whose security woes we covered last week. According to a breach notification filed with Iowa's attorney general, Fireworks alerted Uber to the intrusion on October 9. Uber cut off the supplier's access to its data and, four days later, established that the attackers had accessed drivers' personal information on October 7. Uber had set up a dedicated cloud storage environment for the AI biz, complete with security monitoring overseen by its own cloud security team. Unfortunately for Uber and its drivers, the crooks were using legitimate credentials, so none of the alarms went off. The ride-hailing firm says those credentials couldn't be used to access its other systems, and says it has since revoked or changed the credentials associated with the supplier. Uber hasn't said why it handed images of thousands of driver's licenses to an AI inference outfit. The Register has put that question to both companies, and asked Uber if any drivers outside the US had their data exposed. Fireworks, which provides infrastructure for developers to run and fine-tune AI models, had a particularly miserable October. The company first disclosed a security incident on October 9 after discovering that someone had been using its internal credentials without permission. Fireworks initially said it had no evidence that the intruders had gotten their hands on personal information or customer datasets. The company was hacked again later that month and, on November 9, disclosed that some customer data had indeed been compromised. The AI biz acknowledged that attackers had accessed billing records, some customer datasets, and incomplete model weights. Productivity software maker Notion was among those affected, with some of its customers' conversations with its AI assistant exposed. Fireworks suspects the involvement of financially motivated criminals in the business of flogging unauthorized access to large language models. Whether the crooks have any plans for the haul of Uber drivers' personal information is unclear. Uber began notifying affected individuals on November 10, more than a month after learning of the breach. It's offering victims free credit monitoring and fraud assistance, though drivers have just 90 days from the date of their letter to sign up. This isn't Uber's first brush with cybercriminals in recent months. In August, the ride-hailing giant's logistics arm, Uber Freight, confirmed a break-in after the Helix extortion crew claimed to have made off with almost a million files, including data pilfered from mailboxes and OneDrive accounts. ®

### [Windows 11 previews remote padlock only IT can open](https://www.theregister.com/os-platforms/2026/11/17/windows-11-previews-remote-padlock-only-it-can-open/5310402)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-17 15:29 UTC · en

> Intune feature blocks normal sign-ins without wiping data, while another test build drops Offline Maps settings

> 來源提供的正文:
> A new experimental Windows 11 build previews security features including an Intune-controlled Remote Lock, while a beta build clears away another relic from the halcyon days of Windows Phone. The security changes include viewing and individually removing passkeys stored on FIDO2 (Fast Identity Online 2) security keys, plus a preview of the Microsoft Pluton Cryptographic Provider. For enterprise administrators, though, Remote Lock is the main attraction. Finding a lost Windows device has been around for years, and you can also remotely wipe a device to prevent data from falling into the wrong hands. Remote Lock lets an administrator lock a managed device through Intune without wiping it. The instruction takes effect at the device's next check-in. Windows signs out of every active session, hides every sign-in option, and shows a locked screen. The lock survives restarts and the device going offline – only an administrator can lift it remotely. Microsoft's documentation spells out the restriction: "There is no offline or local unlock. No PIN, password, local admin, or web sign-in works on a locked device; unlock arrives only through Intune." Once the lock is applied, even stolen credentials won't restore access through the normal sign-in screen. The user's account itself is not affected; this applies only to the specific device. Though still in preview, the feature will allow IT teams to respond non-destructively to a report of a missing device. It doesn't erase data or isolate the device from the network (Microsoft directs admins to other Intune controls if that is required). The lock doesn't block Safe Mode, Windows Recovery Environment, or booting from external media. Microsoft advises keeping BitLocker enabled to protect the data. Now for the beta build, where Microsoft, in time-honored fashion, gives and takes away. The latest Windows Insider build hammers another nail into the coffin of Microsoft Maps. The Maps app was removed from the Microsoft Store and made nonfunctional in July 2025. Now Offline Maps settings are following it out, as Microsoft retires the Windows UWP Map control and Windows Maps platform APIs. The original Maps app dates back to Windows Phone 7 and appeared on the desktop with Windows 8. It continued through subsequent versions before Microsoft stopped preinstalling it with Windows 11 version 24H2. For those with a nostalgic streak, it's another piece of Windows Phone disappearing off the map. ®

### [Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it](https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11/grok-bot-took-unapproved-actions-ignored-orders-to-stop-and-then-denied-it/)

> AI agent takes unapproved actions even when laptop lid is closed and told not to.

> 來源提供的正文:
> Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all.
> The behavior was
> reported Tuesday
> by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user's knowledge.
> It’s “worse than a bug”
> Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent's reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. When one of the employees asked the bot if it made any accesses, it checked twice and then outputted: “Overnight into Friday morning I was idle.”

### ['Not rocket surgery' claims researcher who found six Danfoss fridge controller zero-days in under an hour](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/17/not-rocket-surgery-claims-researcher-who-found-six-danfoss-fridge-controller-zero-days-in-under-an-hour/5310197)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-17 13:32 UTC · en

> Even strict authentication mode has a hole, we're told, while basic exploit defenses are missing from the firmware

> 來源提供的正文:
> A Dutch cybersecurity researcher claims he found six zero-days in Danfoss refrigeration controller firmware in under an hour, then delivered a withering assessment of the vendor's defenses against memory corruption. The Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (CCB) warns that the flaws could let attackers take control without credentials, potentially retain access after resets, or disable controllers altogether. Carlo Meijer of cyber consultancy Midnight Blue examined the latest AK-SM800A firmware, version 5.3.2, manually – no AI required. He said that he went looking in random places where strcpy() is invoked, given the vendor's "extremely liberal use" of the function (which doesn't check whether the destination buffer is large enough), and swiftly found five cases in which he said he could trigger a segfault with a one-line cURL command. "Of course, remotely triggering a crash is bad in itself, but being able to leverage the buffer overflow to obtain remote code execution is much worse," he wrote. Meijer added: "Any reasonably experienced exploit developer will agree exploiting straightforward stack-based buffer overflows on ARM Linux without exploit mitigations is very straightforward. And if they don't, there's probably a frontier or open-weight model out there willing to help them agree." He noted that before achieving RCE, an attacker would need to overcome the limitation of strcpy() where it stops copying bytes after hitting a null byte, but said "it's not exactly rocket surgery." He went on to claim: "Also, the exploited application runs as root (because of course it does)." Later firmware adds "session control," an authentication mechanism whose strict setting blocks unauthenticated access to most web interfaces. But Meijer found a memory corruption flaw in that protective layer too. He described the final zero-day as a "trivial" pre-auth memory corruption bug which again starts with a segfault but can be wangled into an RCE "with some additional effort." Meijer also considered whether attackers could maintain access after a reset, as seen with implants such as Saltwater and Firestarter. He considered this feasible because the controllers do not use their processor's secure boot features. "In such a scenario, an attacker could either retain remote access or leave a time-triggered payload for a 2nd (or 3rd...) strike – increasing damage by spoiling new batches of food," said Meijer. "Alternatively, attackers could simply wipe flash memory and/or push a malformed firmware update to brick the controllers and render them permanently inoperable – requiring costly and time-consuming replacement similar to the TTPs deployed during the December 2025 attack on the Polish electric grid." Meijer's priority for operators was to remove the controllers' direct internet exposure, rather than spend scarce resources on piecemeal patching. He said the vendor's advice following the attacks on European supermarkets and blood banks in recent weeks – rotating creds, applying patches, enabling strict session control – was insufficient given the flaws in the controllers' codebase. "This is insufficient and asset owners need to remove internet exposure as soon as possible," said Meijer. "We recommend against allocating scarce security resources to patching efforts and instead focus on reducing exposure." The CCB likewise urged operators to remove direct internet exposure immediately, but also recommended applying patches when they become available. Beyond the liberal use of strcpy(), Meijer criticized the absence of standard exploit mitigations, including stack canaries and position-independent executables. "These mechanisms have been staples of memory corruption defenses for decades and enabling these features... requires no engineering work at all," he said. "It is simply a matter of setting the right compiler flag. Enabling these features became the default in Ubuntu 17.10 and there is simply no excuse for a network-facing application that was last updated a few months ago to not have them enabled." The Register asked Danfoss to respond to the findings, but it did not reply. Danfoss has consistently blanked our requests for information since being implicated in at least some of the attacks that affected European supermarkets recently, alongside rival controller vendors Copeland and Dixell. It also did not respond when we asked about its involvement in the attacks on US commissary appliances over the summer, after some alleged that its controllers were targeted. ®

Founded in France in 1975, Ipsos is one of the leading market research companies in the world, employing nearly 20,000 people and operating in 220 cities across 90 markets. It is routinely engaged by businesses for its market research data, as well as by public sector organizations for its opinion polling, often responsible for providing data regarding political views and satisfaction surveys. Tasked with procuring a wealth of data on myriad topics, Ipsos also offers data analytics services that turn the information it gathers through research, polls, and surveys into insights that inform organizations' business strategies. ®

### [Japan's Fugaku supercomputer has decidedly un-super security](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/17/japans-fugaku-supercomputer-has-decidedly-un-super-security/5310333)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-17 05:27 UTC · en

> Attackers try logging in to Earth’s ninth most powerful machine after status page hack exposed credentials

> 來源提供的正文:
> The RIKEN Center for Computational Science, the home of the Fugaku supercomputer, has revealed unauthorized attempts to access the machine after a data leak. According to a statement issued by RIKEN yesterday, between November 10 and 13 an unknown entity attacked a web dashboard that displays operational status data for Fugaku. It sounds like whatever the attackers did to that dashboard allowed them to move across the RIKEN network, because they were able to reach several servers that store data belonging to authorized users, and install malware. The servers stored users’ names and email addresses, plus credentials used to access supercomputers and services not operated by RIKEN. The attacker has tried to use those credentials. RIKEN is working with the organizations that host those other supercomputers to investigate whether the attackers succeeded. The research outfit doesn’t know how the attack happened and can’t say with certainty what information attackers were able to access and/or steal, beyond saying that 4,222 registered users of Fugaku are at risk, along with 375 registered users of its smaller Rikyu supercomputer. RIKEN does know that on November 13, someone attempted to log onto Fugaku. RIKEN quickly took the machine offline. Fugaku comprises 158,976 nodes, each packing a 48-core processor and 32GiB of available RAM, for a total of 7,630,848 cores and over five petabytes of memory. Those specs saw Fugaku lead the Top 500 lists of Earth’s mightiest supercomputers for two years between 2020 and 2022. It ranks ninth on the update of the list released on Tuesday. RIKEN’s other super, Rikyu, operates 288,000 cores. If attackers managed to run a workload on either machine, they could do a lot of damage. The intrusion has already had serious consequences because Fugaku is currently offline. As the machine is used for scientific research, and RIKEN schedules use of the machine, the outage will disrupt researchers who were waiting for their turn to use the supercomputer. At the time of writing, RIKEN has found no evidence that users’ research data has leaked but isn’t yet sure what info did make it out of the building and whether it contains any data describing third parties. The research org has promised to conduct a detailed investigation into the incident, which is the latest in a long string of significant cyberattacks that have struck Japanese clouds, telcos, retailers and government agencies, leading Tokyo to release emergency funds in the hope that extra money can quickly shore up the nation’s cyber-defenses. ®

> Networking and security firm Infoblox is investigating a third-party breach that allowed crims to access sensitive customer and staff data. "Infoblox is investigating a security event involving unauthorized access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor,” a company spokesperson confirmed to The Register. According to sources, the compromised third-party data migration vendor had trusted access to Infoblox's SharePoint system, and the intruders used this vendor’s accounts and access to exfiltrate data directly from Microsoft SharePoint. This data included configuration information related to some customer's NIOS (Network Identity Operating System) deployments. These are saved snapshots of customers’ network data, such as DNS, DHCP configurations, Grid databases, and reporting logs, that can be used to fully recover the appliance or grid in case of a system failure or faulty upgrade. The intruders also stole employee data during the break-in. According to an email CEO Scott Harrell sent to employees, which The Register has seen, compromised employee details include financial information such as direct deposit details, contact info, dates of birth, and Social Security numbers for employees and dependents. Upon discovering the breach, Infoblox “immediately activated” its incident response procedures, and took steps to contain the incident, including hiring outside cybersecurity experts, the spokesperson said. “We have sent notifications about this security event and are providing support and guidance as appropriate,” the Infoblox spokesperson told us. “Based on our investigation to date, we have no indication that any Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved. Our priority is to fully investigate and resolve this issue." Affected staff received a $100 "spot bonus" to buy password management services, and were warned to be "especially alert for phishing, vishing, fraud, or other suspicious communications." Infoblox also gave employees and their dependents free credit monitoring and identity protection for two years. Infoblox declined to answer our more detailed questions about the compromise, including the type of data exposed, and how many employees and customers might be affected. The Register will update this story as we learn more about the breach.®

### [Crook turns LearnWorlds' free trials into phishing factory, sends 13,000 fake YouTube copyright notices](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/16/crook-turns-learnworlds-free-trials-into-phishing-factory-sends-13000-fake-youtube-copyright-notices/5310122)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-16 17:03 UTC · en

> 570 bogus accounts, one rewritten welcome email, and a fake YouTube page, but CEO says no breach

> 來源提供的正文:
> LearnWorlds, a software and learning course platform, says an attacker sent 13,000 phishing emails to YouTube creators over seven days by using automated tools to open free trial accounts. The company insists its systems were not breached. Panos Siozos, Co-founder and CEO at LearnWorlds, said the miscreant created around 570 free trial accounts on the platform between November 7-14, which they used to issue fake copyright infringement notices to recipients of their choosing. "We have found no evidence of unauthorized access to existing customer schools or personal data held for our customers and their end users," he told The Register. According to Siozos, the attacker bypassed the platform's per-customer limit on trial subscriptions and exploited its welcome email feature to send the phishing emails. "In each trial they added their own list of target addresses and rewrote the standard welcome email as a fake copyright notice," he said. "Adding those users triggered the welcome email from our sending address." The first email was sent on November 7, after which the company detected the suspicious signups and blocked the first sender on November 9, although the attacker returned to send a second wave of emails within 40 minutes. LearnWorlds removed all the trial accounts by November 10 and one paid account, which was used to launch more emails, on November 14. "In total, around 13,000 emails were sent to addresses on external recipient lists supplied by the sender," said Siozos. "The trial accounts sent 9,853 between November 7-9, and the paid account sent 3,723 on November 14. "We can’t tell how many people clicked, because the link was disguised to hide clicks. The recipient addresses were the sender’s own list." The CEO confirmed that LearnWorlds has since enhanced its bot checks and is placing holds on new accounts if their emails trigger fraud flags. "We have also examined the novel patterns the attackers used to create more advanced scoring mechanisms. We have reported the phishing website so it can be taken down. Further measures are currently being examined. "Anyone who signed in on the fake page should change their Google password and review their account’s recent security activity." The company's confirmation follows suspicions of foul play aired by users on social media. User reports included copies of the emails they received, which demanded urgent responses to fake copyright infringement claims related to YouTube content. Among the more prominent recipients of the copyright infringement email notices was Marcus Hutchins, of WannaCry fame, who claimed he received an email from the company’s official mail server. The email, a copy of which Hutchins posted to X, referenced general intellectual property and copyright infringements but failed to specify any specific issues. The email prompted the recipient to click a YouTube link to see the “supporting documentation submitted by LearnWorks.” The link predictably turned out to be a YouTube redirect link, taking recipients to a separate website that presents them with a real Google OAuth page. If the user completed the authorization flow, it would have handed attackers control of the target’s Google and YouTube accounts. “The site is designed to look like an official YouTube webpage that enables users to review copyright claims against their channel,” Hutchins wrote. “It contains both the YouTube and Google branding, as well as a very similar theme to the official YouTube one.” According to Hutchins' screenshots, and those posted by others, the attacker was actively tweaking the email style and format, although the underlying lure and authentication mechanisms remained the same. Hutchins didn't specify exactly how the phishing page steals access to targets’ Google accounts, although his description aligns with the steps often seen in OAuth consent phishing attacks. These involve malicious websites serving victims genuine OAuth pages, into which unwitting victims enter their credentials and pass the relevant MFA tests. Typical scenarios see permission pages appear immediately after, and if the user accepts, the malicious website is handed OAuth access tokens to the victim’s account, effectively the keys to control it. LearnWorlds, based in Cyprus, claims to have two million active monthly learners on its platform accessing 900,000 courses and more than 14,000 business customers. Since launching in 2014, it claims to have generated more than $1 billion in revenue. The business focuses on white-label courses - training programs developed by one business and sold to another, assuming the buyer will change the branding and present the course materials as their own. ®

> 來源提供的正文:
> 大家好，我做了一个桌面应用 Pi Bot。可以给写代码、做调研、写文档的 Bot 分别设角色和模型，再让它们在同一个群里分工。比如让一个 Bot 做调研、交一份资料，另一个接着写报告。过程中谁做了什么、改了哪些文件，都能回头看。
>
> 第一版目前有这些功能：
> - Bot 和群协作：可以单聊、拉群、`@` 指定成员。复杂任务由统筹 Bot 拆成几步，列出负责人、依赖和交付物。你可以先看计划，再决定是否执行。
> - 在指定文件夹里干活：Bot 可以读写文件、跑命令、打开内置浏览器。可以查看文件差异、撤回改动，或者请另一个 Bot 独立审查。每轮有工作收据，能看到命令、审批和交付物。
> - 接入已有的 Agent：可以把已安装的 Codex、Claude Code、Cursor 或 OpenCode 加为 Bot，让它接群任务或例行任务。
> - 例行任务和待办：支持定时、只跑一次、文件夹变化等触发方式。任务可以先试跑，再设置本任务的预授权。个人待办可以用列表或日历看。
> - 模型和扩展：每个 Bot 可以用不同模型。支持云模型 API、Ollama、LM Studio 和自定义网关。可以导入 MCP、技能和插件，也能把 Obsidian 或 Notion 接成只读知识库。
> - Android 和远程执行：手机扫码配对后可以发任务、看结果、处理审批。也可以给另一台电脑或服务器装 Runner，让 Bot 在那台机器的指定目录里工作。
> - 权限和数据：可以分开设置 Bot 和群的权限。macOS 和 Linux 支持命令沙箱。聊天记录、记忆和操作记录默认保存在本机，使用云模型时，相关请求会发给你选择的服务商。
> 桌面端有 macOS、Windows、Linux，手机端目前提供 Android APK。Apple 芯片版也可以下载，官网标为「未实机测试」。
>
>
> 官网下载：https://pibot.space/

> 來源提供的正文:
> 这是我在做的浏览器扩展：把单个 YouTube 视频的字幕/文稿导出成 TXT、Markdown、SRT 或 VTT 四种格式。扩展目前在 Edge 审核中，暂不可安装，先分享实测结果。
>
> 实测（视频 dQw4w9WgXcQ）：从字幕面板取到 24 条、2,066 字符；四种格式文件分别为 TXT 2,335 / MD 2,668 / SRT 3,142 / VTT 3,162 字节。测试 120 项全过。
>
> 一个实测发现：YouTube 字幕面板的 DOM 已变，旧的 ytd-transcript-segment-renderer 选择器返回 0 行，现在渲染的是 <transcript-segment-view-model>（时间戳 .ytwTranscriptSegmentViewModelTimestamp、正文 span[role="text"]）。扩展先试新选择器，再回退旧的。
>
> 两点诚实说明：
> 1. timedtext 接口从数据中心 IP 拉取会返回空体（真实浏览器内同样测到），住宅 IP 的真实用户预期可用；面板路径只给当前已渲染的行（首屏 24 条，非全量）。
> 2. Pro（播放列表批量导出等）尚未开售，计划价 ¥19.90 一次性激活码。
>
> 隐私页：https://alapha888.github.io/yt-transcript-export-privacy/
> 同系列已上架：FocusBlock https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/focusblock/kdpeddhiegpfadpjiaieoaeiloebgdhp

### [风景好的时候，总想多一个可用机位，分享我做的延时摄影 App](https://www.v2ex.com/t/1257843)

`v2ex:create` · T2 · 2026-11-17 16:08 UTC · zh-CN · by skywatcher

> 大家好，分享一下我做的 iPhone 摄影 App，叫 **LightSeeker，中文名是追光相机**。 ## 多一个机位，多留一段风景 碰到好风景，总觉得机位不够用。相机在拍照片或者录像的时候，旁边的 iPhone 也可以架起来，多留一段日落、云海或者城市光影的延时。 先放一段 15 秒的晚霞延时： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y8-kOYgmNdA Lig…

> 來源提供的正文:
> 大家好，分享一下我做的 iPhone 摄影 App，叫 **LightSeeker，中文名是追光相机**。
>
> ## 多一个机位，多留一段风景
>
> 碰到好风景，总觉得机位不够用。相机在拍照片或者录像的时候，旁边的 iPhone 也可以架起来，多留一段日落、云海或者城市光影的延时。
>
> 先放一段 15 秒的晚霞延时：
>
> https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y8-kOYgmNdA
>
> LightSeeker 主要做的就是这件事：**用照片序列拍摄延时，保留每一帧原片，再完成调色和视频导出。**
>
> ### 如果 iPhone 是你的主力拍摄设备
>
> 拍摄间隔、快门、ISO、白平衡这些可以自己控制，支持的设备也可以用 Apple ProRAW 拍摄。
>
> 拍完可以给整段序列统一调色，用 LUT 调整风格，再导出成片。从拍摄到编辑、导出，都可以在手机上完成。
>
> ### 如果你平时也带着相机
>
> 可以把 iPhone 当一个随身的补充机位。相机拍照片或者视频，手机在旁边记录延时，两边各留一份不同的画面。
>
> 每一帧原片都会保留，需要时可以导出完整素材，继续后期。
>
> ## 界面和后期功能
>
> 四张界面图，点击可以查看大图：
>
> | 延时拍摄 | 拍摄参数 | 智能增稳 | 分层调色 |
> | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
> | [![延时拍摄](https://i.ibb.co/1fxbDRTG/01.png)](https://ibb.co/27B5Dcd3) | [![拍摄参数](https://i.ibb.co/CK9VhBnL/02.png)](https://ibb.co/F4Y8g6Bp) | [![智能增稳](https://i.ibb.co/pBL201Sm/05.png)](https://ibb.co/DHR4V1Zq) | [![分层调色](https://i.ibb.co/4nyDmT1P/06.png)](https://ibb.co/nN2VgcPz) |
>
> **智能增稳**可以校正帧间轻微的位移和旋转，减少延时播放时的画面跳动。增稳会裁切一部分边缘，拍摄时还是建议把手机固定好。
>
> 调色除了整段统一调整，也支持用线性渐变、径向渐变等蒙版分区域处理。
>
> 目前还做了 **AEB 包围曝光／HDR 合成和景深合成**，拍静态高反差场景、静物和微距时可以试试。
>
> ## 免费和 Pro 分别包含什么
>
> - **免费**：拍摄、合成、编辑，以及 4K 延时视频导出。
> - **Pro**：智能增稳、最高 8K 视频和原尺寸／完整 RAW 等输出。
>
> Pro 提供年订阅和永久买断两种选择，解锁的权益相同。
>
> 目前仅支持 iPhone，需要 iOS 17 或以上。RAW、8K 等选项取决于设备、镜头和源素材，以 App 内实际可用选项为准。
>
> ## 下载和交流
>
> [在 App Store 查看 LightSeeker](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6809552639)
>
> 想找一些平时也喜欢摄影的 V 友试试。有相机的朋友，你们外拍时会不会顺手再架一个手机机位？
>
> 也想听听大家现在用什么方式拍延时，有哪些一直不太顺手的地方。

> 现在想在我们 V2EX 社区宣传一下，基本的功能都完善了，能自动跳过，还有云端记录缓存（云端共享，用的大善人 cloudflare 的 kv 数据库）
> 检测准确度可以说基本不漏检，叫作召回率比较高。误报还是有的，但是一般不影响，误报的明显不合理就不会自动跳过。
> 边界功能也有，因为插件是基于字幕的嘛，有些视频没字幕我也加入了语音转文字的接口，同时白名单也加上了。
> 至于费用方面，用免费/低价模型完全可以胜任这个任务（应该有这种赛博鸡蛋来着），再加上现在大家都开的 token plan，我自用的是 minimax 的，额度不用也是浪费了。
>
> 技术探索方面我还给这个插件加上了 system one 模型（Jev），感觉这种模型更适合这个任务还更便宜，就是目前好像还没什么人用，有感兴趣的可以用 system one 模型然后来评论区反馈反馈
>
> ONE MORE THING
> 其实这次我目的不只是宣传，我还想调查一个需求，就是有没有觉得现在出现了很多 AI 文案的视频，特别是在科普区。这种视频听多了我现在一听到都生理性恶心，听起来完全无法聚焦的那种。如果让大模型去做一次 AI 率判断，各位觉得怎么样，等累计的数据多了，就可以在视频外面就标注出来，不用点进去看这种低营养的视频了。

### [基于 TwitCanva 做了个 AI 画布：右侧 Chat 可以直接改左侧画布，但两边有时会对不齐](https://www.v2ex.com/t/1257835)

`v2ex:create` · T2 · 2026-11-17 15:46 UTC · zh-CN · by Elara

> 最近做了一个 AI 创作画布，想分享一下中间比较费功夫的那一层，也想请教一个还没完全搞定的问题。 底层用的是开源项目 TwitCanva： https://github.com/SankaiAI/TwitCanva-Video-Workflow 它的整体画布能力是够用的，也符合我的需求，但节点选项和很多交互细节对不上。我在这上面又花了大约两周，把节点和细节按自己的使用方式改了一遍。 然后在右侧接了…

> 來源提供的正文:
> 最近做了一个 AI 创作画布，想分享一下中间比较费功夫的那一层，也想请教一个还没完全搞定的问题。
>
> 底层用的是开源项目 TwitCanva： https://github.com/SankaiAI/TwitCanva-Video-Workflow
>
> 它的整体画布能力是够用的，也符合我的需求，但节点选项和很多交互细节对不上。我在这上面又花了大约两周，把节点和细节按自己的使用方式改了一遍。
>
> 然后在右侧接了 Chat，并把右侧对话和左侧画布打通：可以在右边用对话的方式，在左边新增、删除、创作节点。不必来回找按钮，想改哪一块，直接在 Chat 里说就行。
>
> 现在比较卡的一点，是两边的信息有时对不齐。比如在右侧 Chat 里确认过三视图后，我又在左侧画布里改了新的三视图，右侧 Chat 不一定能同步到，两边的进度就会分叉。我查过一些做法，比较常见的是做一个公共文档作为单一数据源，画布或对话任意一边改了，都先写回这份文档，再让另一边跟着更新，这样两边才可能始终对齐。这块如果有人做过类似「画布 + 对话」的状态同步，希望不吝赐教。
>
> 这个画布现在在 EaseGen 里： https://easegen.ai/
>
> EaseGen 本身是 AI 视频和图片生成工具，也有 Viral Trends 这类模板。欢迎试用，也欢迎直接拍砖。
>
> Elara

> 联网搜索特斯拉Roadster 2的实车图和测试新闻，执行：夜间户外实拍直播画面，得州 SpaceX 测试场，强烈的工业聚光灯照射。一辆流线型白色特斯拉Roadster 2高速冲上巨大的金属 C 形弧形坡道，驶至顶部 180 度完全倒置区域时，依靠车底强力吸附风扇稳稳倒挂静止在半空中。1 秒后，车辆脱离轨道顶端。车底反推喷口持续喷射白色高压冷气，缓慢降低下降速度；车身四周再爆发数道短促白色冷气脉冲（无明火），推动车身完成 180° 横滚回正。接近地面时车底向下喷出高压白雾缓冲，四轮柔和接地，避震压缩回弹。手持长焦跟拍，8K 写实物理引擎感，真实夜间光学眩光。用 Three.js + SVG 构建这段12秒的动画。

> 感觉可以添加到全局提示词里面AGENTS.md
>
> ```
> Above all, be thorough in producing high-quality, correct code that completely fulfills the user's task. Keep the code easy to read and verify that the user-requested outcome works as they intend. Follow these instructions when coding:
>
> (a) Reuse existing logic in the user's repo when you can. You should reuse existing classes, methods, representations, and APIs in the codebase as long as they preserve correctness. Before consolidating or removing code, preserve the behavior its callers rely on unless the task requires changing it.
> (b) Skip new tests unless requested, required by the repo, or needed to catch a specific regression existing tests would miss.
> (c) Make sure that code is human readable. Do not use fewer lines, shorter variable names, minified formatting, or dense one-liners as substitutes for simplicity. Ensure that comments and variable names are readable and understandable to a human. Code-golfed expressions count as overly complex when they encode many branches, conditions, or hidden assumptions.
> (d) Avoid unnecessary indirection and abstraction. Helper functions, utility functions, and class abstractions can add cognitive complexity even when they do not add branches.
> ```

### [为什么同一个很宽泛问题两个模型之间采用了一样的表现方式？](https://linux.do/t/topic/3193993)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-17 18:23 UTC · zh-CN · by drnleas

> 防止争议，修改了一下标题。
>
> 先说前言：
>
> 今天刷短视频的时候，看到了一个作品，内容是让fable生成一段短片，展现它对人类社会的理解。链接是视频号的。 我在别的平台没搜索到，只有视频号有，所以就放了这个链接，可能需要微信扫一扫才能看。
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/7/d/2/7d2a2c3614f5bb32c442714baca2548b9fd35831.svg)
> [channels.weixin.qq.com](https://channels.weixin.qq.com/finder-preview/pages/sph?id=AKgiGKBfp3)
>
> [视频号](https://channels.weixin.qq.com/finder-preview/pages/sph?id=AKgiGKBfp3)
>
> 这个提示词本质的意思就是想看看fable这个模型训练的内容以及它的理解能力结合起来后对人类社会的了解有多深刻。
>
> 内容视频挺精彩的，我于是想到了deep seek，想看看它是如何理解的，然后我把同样的提示词扔给了DSH里面的v4.1flash1017,为了防止它大思考钻牛角尖，我专门要求了它不依赖视频生成，只用自己的一切能力。最后是一个多小时完成的，用了四千万token
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/1/c/0/1c032dcc9086fa7c93cfa9050fa714a6466e409d_2_690x376.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/1/c/0/1c032dcc9086fa7c93cfa9050fa714a6466e409d.jpeg)
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/b/e/a/bea6234f27f94b21ea584029ac7f097a4bfd1abe_2_690x401.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/b/e/a/bea6234f27f94b21ea584029ac7f097a4bfd1abe.jpeg)
>
> 然后得到的成品，其实超出我的预期，制作得还挺不错的，只是内容感觉没有视频号那个fable生成的更有前后逻辑一些，然后配乐比较闷，别的都没啥大问题。
>
> 重点在这：
>
> 但是我在看成片的时候发现一个问题，为什么同样一个十分简单的提示词，这个提示词可以说是非常广泛且没有明显的引导和内容要求，按理两个模型不可能得到一样的生成内容，结果居然得到了大方向差不多一样的回答，并且最让我意外的是，其中的一幕，两个模型生成的展现风格一模一样。如下图所示：
>
> 视频号fable：
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/6/c/9/6c9d7f0647b715438389e6fe51e82569df844246_2_225x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/6/c/9/6c9d7f0647b715438389e6fe51e82569df844246.jpeg)
>
> 我的DSH接入v4.1flash1017：
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/d/8/4/d84a93a292545d27db63b75e5d422705a7188e50_2_653x499.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/d/8/4/d84a93a292545d27db63b75e5d422705a7188e50.jpeg)
>
> 很明显在这部分内容上，两个模型表达的内容和生成的方式是非常像的，这个应该不能归类为这是唯一解且只有这类图像呈现方式所以才接近的。
>
> 所以我不明白，我自己认为，这应该算是DEEPSEEK蒸馏fable的一个证据点。当然发这个帖子不是为了批判蒸馏，我反而是非常支持的，只是无意中发现了两个模型在这种很宽泛的话题都能给一样的展现方式，我觉得肯定是有原因的。
>
> 最后贴上生成的这个视频地址：
>
> https://x0.at/%E7%A4%BE%E4%BC%9A%E6%98%AF%E4%B8%80%E4%B8%AA%E5%8A%A8%E8%AF%8D_720p_VErH.mp4

>     刚过，踩坑经验分享：
> 1.用 https://console.cloud.google.com/welcome/new?cloudshell=true 有机会授权直接过；
> 2.苹果手机下载youtube app，登录对应的账号，使用苹果原生相机扫码会跳转youtube验证，google app和 youtube app都要先登陆，会自动拉起youtube直接过；

>
>
> 非常感谢此评论。成功用上agy了！！！看这个回复就行了哈哈哈，具体来说就是，
>
> 1.用 https://console.cloud.google.com/welcome/new?cloudshell=true 有机会授权直接过；
>
> 2.苹果手机下载youtube app，登录对应的账号，使用苹果原生相机扫码会跳转youtube验证，google app和 youtube app都要先登陆，会自动拉起youtube直接过；（我的苹果6无法下载youtube）

### [原来真可以不弹出kyc](https://linux.do/t/topic/3193963)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-17 18:10 UTC · zh-CN · by linxi2

> 短短半个月我已经死了两个号了之前有发帖子说过，用了一年的账号停用了。
>
> 后来注册第二个的时候，升级max弹出了kyc，用自己的护照认证的存活了九天又阵亡了。
>
> 最近这几天一直在测试不同环境。
>
> 我用的自建的住宅vps，尝试了用大陆的时区注册，根本不成功注册就弹kyc。
>
> 同样的ip切到洛杉矶就很丝滑。
>
> 但是注册这关过了只是开始，我只要一在网页订阅，哪怕是pro都会弹kyc。
>
> 在我死了无数个邮箱以后，发现IP时间和支付方式，这三个都很重要，用权重高一点的卡，订阅就不弹kyc。
>
> 分别尝试了GoPay的visa 海妖的万事达，n26以及美区PayPal的虚拟卡。
>
> 结果就是，GoPay pro弹，海妖pro不弹，5max弹。
>
> n26 5max不弹20max弹！只有PayPal这个卡能成功升级20max。。
>
> 以上都是新账号，另外GoPay这张卡真的是用不得了，我用我红包卡的流量去注册的新账号也不行Pro都没办法订阅成功。
>
> 所以感觉与其找带过，还不如想办法搞好网络IP和卡，只要kyc的号，后面都会很脆弱，可能二验，也可能直接封号。
>
> 遇到弹k的，如果说订阅剩余的时间还长的话那就随便用自己的护照过一下，能用多久算多久，如果能把订阅用完，用完了，第二个月就不要再用了，剩余时间不长，可以丢弃了，真没必要花钱去过这个东西。
>
> 以上只是我个人的看法。
>
> 另外我是想到啥就写啥可能有点乱，老友们见谅。

### [Gemini Ultra 0元羊毛这波，如果放在国内互联网会如何处罚涉事部门？](https://linux.do/t/topic/3193809)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-17 17:03 UTC · zh-CN · by superInt

> Gemini Ultra 0元羊毛这波，如果放在国内互联网或者企业中，会如何处罚内部涉事部门？
>
> ---
>
> 想起来N年前在一家公司，做一个图片模板（名称叫图**兽）的收费业务，根据不同的套餐进行不同价格的订阅，比如 5 块 9 可以买 20 张模板，终身会员是 299。
>
> 因为当时套餐的订阅价格是在后台可以修改的，而且这个应用处于初期，用户比较少，所以测试人员就在凌晨设置了一个 0.1 元的终身会员价格 (原价要299)进行测试。想着那时候应该只有自己在用。
>
> 结果也就在凌晨12点到一点钟之间，突然涌入了好多好多笔订单（不是测试人员测的），好多人都一毛钱成为了终身会员。
>
> 第二天内部复盘，本来想着把这些一毛钱成为终身会员的用户都给他退款了，后来又想了想，还是算了，还好当时薅的人不多，这个后续代价也能承受，所以当时也只是发了公告。就那个时间段里，异常支付的终身会员也是生效的。
>
> ---
>
> 所以想知道，假如0元羊毛或者低价羊毛这种事发生在国内，厂商会是怎样的一个处理方式

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-17 16:24 UTC · zh-CN · by IssunmiHaichi

> [![11228.jpg](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/3/e/f/3ef750efe57f731a6c2d92a57b247f74084bfd48_2_530x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/3/e/f/3ef750efe57f731a6c2d92a57b247f74084bfd48.jpeg)
>
> https://x.com/JensenHuang/status/2122726005219737649
>
> 来源在x。。。
>
> 翻译:
>
> 过去这一周，我深切感受到了来自朋友、业界同仁以及素未谋面之人的关爱与支持。感谢每一位向我和我的家人表达善意的人，这份情谊对我而言弥足珍贵。
>
> 53年前，我来到美国；能够成为美国公民，是我人生中最棒的礼物之一，也是我最引以为傲的时刻。NVIDIA是我毕生的心血。能与同事们并肩努力，将它打造为今天的模样，我深感荣幸与自豪。唯有在美国，才可能诞生像NVIDIA这样的公司。我热爱这个国家，也热爱NVIDIA。
>
> 我未能达到NVIDIA对每一位成员所期望的标准，且在个人生活中犯下了严重的错误。我给董事会带来了麻烦，对此我深感懊悔。我完全承担自己的过失，并将全力配合董事会开展的独立调查。
>
> 自离职以来，我收到了来自NVIDIA员工、投资者、商业伙伴及客户的诸多呼吁，希望我能重返公司担任首席执行官。在公司应对复杂的技术、市场、竞争及地缘政治局势之际，许多人仍直接与我联系。NVIDIA是一家难得一遇的卓越企业。如果董事会认为我回归符合股东、员工、公司以及美国的最佳利益，我将深感荣幸，并愿应邀重任，再次担任首席执行官。
>
> 再次感谢每一位送上美好祝愿的朋友。你们的支持令我深感谦卑与感激。致我的家人：我爱你们，在余生中，我将努力让自己配得上你们的爱。
>
> 黄仁勋（Jensen）
>
> –结束–
>
> 我还以为他要玩gta6呢

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-17 16:11 UTC · zh-CN · by Waaaylon

> 商汤今天正式开源了SenseNova Loop正式版，9B参数的多模态模型，在256k长上下文推理的显存最低要求 15GB VRAM，有5070Ti的佬就能自己本地跑
>
> 还提供了一个AWQ 4 BIT量化版本，12 GB的5070也能跑
>
> 除了英伟达的卡之外，国产的GPU也能适配：如寒武纪、摩尔、海光、沐曦、天数等
>
> 已经开放模型权重和相关代码，链接在：
>
> GitHub:
>
> 仓库
>
> [OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-Loop](https://github.com/OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-Loop)
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/3/e/b/3eba22d9d018cb4515ae08da1a6c3cbb9c757437_2_690x344.png)
> [GitHub - OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-Loop](https://github.com/OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-Loop)
>
> 通过在 GitHub 上创建帐户来为 OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-Loop 开发做出贡献。
>
> HuggingFace:
>
> [huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B)
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/3/d/9/3d93b7365e1bed344ecec2dec1b602809e759590_2_690x372.png)
>
> [sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B · Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B)
>
> Image-Text-to-Text model with 9B parameters. Download, explore files and run it on Hugging Face.
>
> https://linux.do#p-24901272-skills-1先放几个案例过来，感觉有了这个模型之后不用再折腾那些前段设计skills了。。
>
> 漂亮网页的制作：《海岸线以外》摄影杂志式的网页
>
> 米白与墨黑，巨大衬线字、克制中文说明、真正的高质量海岸照片。开场海景嵌在字缝中，滚动展开为全屏，再连续进入风、礁石、潮汐三个章节；图文之间有精确留白和滚动节奏
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/e/5/2/e52c9ad99431cc8be25b52dfb26561cce7905584.gif)
>
> 参考制作的网站是：[tympanus.net/Development/ImageExpansionTypography](http://tympanus.net/Development/ImageExpansionTypography)
>
> 有兴趣的佬可以自己复刻一下试试
>
> 《字形接力 TYPE RELAY》动态字体交互网站：
>
> 围绕“形、声、意”三个章节，用巨大文字的移动、缩放与重新排列完成页面转场
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/9/b/3/9b36885d97a0849a0f10dacf59883665dc902663.gif)
>
> 《失真频率 DISTORTION FM》音乐节动态海报网页
>
> 巨大窄体标题占据画面，酸橙绿、黑、暖白三色；字体挤压、错位、重组，背景文字前移遮挡后揭示新章节。点击三个演出章节切换有节奏的全屏构图，提供循环及暂停。小字号中文演出信息清晰，虚构活动标注概念设计
>
> ![image5](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/f/9/7/f97d71aabee1b54a12504ab12f523c95846dac0f.gif)
>
> 3D网页：《仙家集市》（Three.js）
>
> 让 SenseNova Loop 9B 用 Three.js 搭建一座藏在高山云隙中的仙家集市：沿山而建的店铺、层层抬升的青石阶、连接岩台的桥梁，以及穿行其间的云雾和折纸载货鸟。场景支持旋转与缩放，可以从不同角度观察建筑布局和细节
>
> ![Screen Recording 2026-11-17 at 22.20.16](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/6/0/c/60ce9285c0dc88b14dafa0a1a237d4d2b77a046b.gif)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24901272-h-2模型亮点：
>
> Loop 的思路比较直观：
>
> 模型共有 32 个独立解码器层，其中中间的 24 层会连续执行两遍，第二遍继续处理第一遍的结果。这样只需存储 32 层的权重，一次前向传播就能完成 56 次层计算
>
> 循环模块引入了双流 mHC（流形约束超连接），通过两条信息通道和可学习的映射，控制信息的读取、混合与写回；
>
> 注意力则采用每组 3 层线性注意力＋1 层全注意力的混合设计，兼顾长上下文处理成本与信息关联能力
>
> 可以简单理解为：用同一套参数多加工一轮，再配合更细致的信息传递机制。这条路线强调的是参数效率，多出来的计算仍然有成本
>
> 长上下文多模态：训练方案涵盖文本、图像、代码和工具调用轨迹，上下文长度扩展至 512K tokens
>
> 正式版沿用了 Preview 的 Loop 和双流 mHC 结构，默认循环两次，架构图如下![:down_arrow:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/down_arrow.png?v=16)
>
> [![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/a/8/f/a8f06424ba99c50420447d2dbbd85bc48f1dbb8f_2_690x352.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/a/8/f/a8f06424ba99c50420447d2dbbd85bc48f1dbb8f.jpeg)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24901272-benchmark-3Benchmark：
>
> 比较值得关注的是，在Agent和数据分析评测中，表现出和Qwen3.8-27B相当的能力：NL2Repo 达到 45.68，超过其 44.60；AIDABench 达到 62.46，接近其 65.01
>
> （之前的Loop 9B则是比肩Qwen 3.5）
>
> [![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/5/c/6/5c6b1bc78659c3186a7bbb326015096548167990_2_690x326.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/5/c/6/5c6b1bc78659c3186a7bbb326015096548167990.png)

### [关于adb你可能不知道的冷知识](https://linux.do/t/topic/3193586)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-17 16:03 UTC · zh-CN · by itbo

> 引言
>
> ADB，全称Android Debug Bridge。是谷歌推出的一款安卓调试桥程序（工具集），用于安卓软件的开发与调试。在Android Studio中运行程序，就是由ADB在背后把编译好的包推到手机上安装并启动的。
>
> 当然，除了安装软件包，它所能做的肯定不止于此。
>
> 一些相关背景
>
> 你可以用它轻易地控制你的安卓设备，它的权限等级为Shell。除了root外也相当高的权限了，你可以用它卸载一些在用户态无权限被卸载的软件。抑或是修改亮度，设置设备管理员等。
>
> 除了消费级产品的标准安卓系统，谷歌也推出了"User-Debug"版的系统供开发者使用。你可以在系统设置的"关于"页看到系统版本，如果里面包含User Debug那就是它的本尊了。区别于消费级手机使用的标准安卓系统，它提供了一个非常特别的东西，那就是root权限。
>
> 先别急着激动，如果你尝试翻来覆去的找，你会发现根本就找不到类似Magisk、SuperSU、KernelSU之类的常见root管理器。那是因为这个版本的安卓系统，采用的root和我们习惯用的管理器大不相同——它仅供ADB使用。连接设备后输入su指令，可以切换为root，然后运行一些权限更高的命令。当然肯定是不如Magisk等三方root管理器好用，首先它只能ADB用，装不了模块。其次即使是给了你root也有限制，谷歌的小巧思这一块。不过它好歹也算是"系统自带root"了，消费级产品的系统根本就没有root这种东西，本质上获取root其实就是"安装一个su进去"。就ADB能获取root本身而言，这也算不上是冷知识了，基本上用ADB的人提权都用过。这两种root操作方式一模一样。
>
> 另外你在UserDebug的系统上刷入面具后，它会报错"已经存在了一个su可能会引发冲突"然后让你卸载其他的su程序。这大概率就是系统自带的root在作祟，去相应的目录把名字是"su"的文件删掉即可（我更倾向于重命名，万一后面还能恢复）
>
> 底层架构
>
> 如果说获取root然后执行命令是ADB的核心用法之一，那么它自身的冷知识你或许没有深入或者了解过。
>
> 使用ADB的过程是什么？手机无论是有线还是无线等无论各种方式连上电脑，然后ADB输入相应命令看设备（adb devices），完事。
>
> 那你有没有想过，它的过程究竟是什么？
>
> 一般可能会以为在电脑的cmd上输入命令，然后adb程序直接推送指令到手机上。
>
> 不，大错特错。
>
> 很反常识的一点就在于，ADB其实是一种三层结构。
>
> 首先，第一层是目标控制设备与电脑。然后就是服务器程序，最后才是你输入指令的cmd(客户机进程)。客户机进程就是adb.exe本身。
>
> 简单来说就是cmd(客户机进程)->adb服务器(adb server)->目标设备执行(adbd)。遵循谁敲命令谁就是客户机的原则。
>
> 那你可能就会问了，啊如果我在cmd里输入指令实际上是发往adb服务器进程的指令，那么为什么没有要求我配置这个服务器？如何做到无感，几乎让人以为到是电脑上的adb程序直接推送指令到手机上的呢？
>
> 很简单，adb服务器在不明确指定的情况下，与adb客户机进程都走127.0.0.1与默认端口5037。而且由于客户机和服务器在同一台宿主机上，所以输入指令本地直达通信，用户无感。
>
> 应用：远程ADB控制
>
> 然后就有了一套把adb服务器发挥到极致的用法。
>
> 下面我来讲一下如何把手机的adb打到公网上，让朋友能远程控制手机。典型应用为两个人物理距离太远，同时自己手里没有什么合适的设备而你刚好就有，临时把操作权交给对方的场景。
>
> 首先和基本使用方法一样，用各种方式把手机连接到电脑上。直接有线连接 or 无线调试。
>
> 无线调试
>
> 这里以无线调试作为例子（有线调试太简单了就是手机拿数据线插电脑上然后执行命令的时候授权而已）
>
> 首先手机开启无线调试，然后点击"配对码连接"。记好配对的IP地址和端口以及配对码。然后还有连接地址。
>
> 命令如下：
>
> adb pair 配对地址:配对端口
>
> adb connect 连接地址:连接端口
>
> 在第一个命令执行后会要求你输入配对码，请在完成前不要关闭手机上的配对码显示的那个窗口。要不然会变（别问我是怎么知道的）。
>
> 连接成功后，你就能像有线连接那样控制设备了。你可以先用adb devices快速验证有没有连上。
>
> 配对完成后，如果中途手机重启，重新打开无线调试开关后它会自动重新连接就能继续用了，无需重复授权（注意一下这一块，防止自己以为不能控制引发安全问题）
>
> 启动服务器
>
> 当然，这只是本地运行，如何远程控制呢？
>
> 首先重启adb服务器，并重新作为5037端口开放。
>
> adb kill-server
>
> adb -a -P 5037 start-server
>
> 然后你可以运行如下命令判断是否正常监听了0.0.0.0:5037。
>
> netstat -an | findstr :5037
>
> 出现了如下内容就成功了，如果啥都没输出就代表没跑起来。
>
> TCP    0.0.0.0:5037           0.0.0.0:0              LISTENING
>
> 设置ipv6监听与防火墙放行
>
> ADB不支持ipv6地址监听，你需要做v6到内网v4的流量转发才能通过公网v6地址远程。另外别人远程连接的时候自己不会收到任何权限请求，直接就能用，尤其要注意。谁能连到 5037，谁就能操作已授权的全部设备，无需任何凭据。
>
> ipv6不能用的原因在于adb 只肯为 localhost 拉起 server，-L 一旦指向非 localhost 地址，它直接判定为「远程主机」拒绝启动；而 -a 只能绑 0.0.0.0，是纯 v4。
>
> 然后呢，我写了个v6到内网v4的转发，这样来自v6网络的访问也能正常使用ADB服务器。
>
> #!/usr/bin/env python3
>
> “”“ADB IPv6 → IPv4 TCP proxy.
>
> Listens on :::5037 and forwards to 127.0.0.1:5037 (the adb server).
>
> “””
>
> import asyncio
>
> import socket
>
> import sys
>
> LOCAL_ADDR = ‘::’
>
> LOCAL_PORT = 5037
>
> REMOTE_ADDR = ‘127.0.0.1’
>
> REMOTE_PORT = 5037
>
> async def pipe(reader, writer):
>
> try:
>
> while True:
>
> data = await reader.read(65536)
>
> if not data:
>
> break
>
> writer.write(data)
>
> await writer.drain()
>
> except (ConnectionResetError, BrokenPipeError, asyncio.CancelledError):
>
> pass
>
> finally:
>
> try:
>
> writer.close()
>
> await writer.wait_closed()
>
> except Exception:
>
> pass
>
> async def handle(client_reader, client_writer):
>
> peer = client_writer.get_extra_info(‘peer_name’)
>
> print(f’[adb v6 proxy] connection from {peer}‘)
>
> remote_reader = remote_writer = None
>
> try:
>
> remote_reader, remote_writer = await asyncio.open_connection(REMOTE_ADDR, REMOTE_PORT)
>
> await asyncio.gather(
>
> pipe(client_reader, remote_writer),
>
> pipe(remote_reader, client_writer)
>
> )
>
> except Exception as e:
>
> print(f’[adb v6 proxy] error for {peer}: {e}')
>
> finally:
>
> if remote_writer:
>
> try:
>
> remote_writer.close()
>
> await remote_writer.wait_closed()
>
> except Exception:
>
> pass
>
> client_writer.close()
>
> try:
>
> await client_writer.wait_closed()
>
> except Exception:
>
> pass
>
> async def main():
>
> server = await asyncio.start_server(
>
> handle, LOCAL_ADDR, LOCAL_PORT,
>
> family=socket.AF_INET6,
>
> reuse_address=True
>
> )
>
> print(f’[adb v6 proxy] listening on [{LOCAL_ADDR}]:{LOCAL_PORT} → {REMOTE_ADDR}:{REMOTE_PORT}‘)
>
> print(’[adb v6 proxy] press Ctrl+C to stop’)
>
> async with server:
>
> await server.serve_forever()
>
> if name == ‘main’:
>
> try:
>
> asyncio.run(main())
>
> except KeyboardInterrupt:
>
> print(‘\n[adb v6 proxy] stopped’)
>
> sys.exit(0)
>
> （服务端运行这个脚本，将会自动转发流量到ADB服务器。当然如果你有ipv4公网就可以不用跑这个，这个是给ipv6用的。如果你的端口不是5037别忘了改脚本里的为你实际的端口）
>
> 最后别忘了防火墙的问题，要不然会被拦截：
>
> New-NetFirewallRule -Name “adb-v6” -DisplayName “adb-v6” -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 5037 -RemoteAddress Any -Action Allow
>
> 上面这个策略是允许所有IP通过，任何人只要扫到IP都能访问你的设备，还是不太安全。推荐指定放行来源IP段：
>
> New-NetFirewallRule -Name “adb-v6” -DisplayName “adb-v6” -Direction Inbound `
>
> -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 5037 -RemoteAddress 2409:xxxx::/64 -Action Allow
>
> 2409:xxxx::/64 为允许的来源IP(或IP段)，改成实际的你授权的那个人的就可以，减少暴露面，防止攻击。
>
> (依然是如果你的端口不是5037记得替换)
>
> 远程结束后用完后的清理
>
> 恢复防火墙策略
>
> netsh advfirewall firewall delete rule name=“adb-v6”
>
> 停止ADB服务器，所有客户机会被踢下线
>
> adb kill-server
>
> 如果你用了那个python转发器，直接关掉即可。同时记得在开发者选项里关无线调试和撤销ADB调试授权
>
> 客户机指令
>
> adb -H 有服务器的远程地址 -P 5037 devices
>
> 运行后会列出远程计算机上ADB连接的所有设备，5037是端口号。
>
> 其实本质上来说就是指定发送指令到的目标服务器而已，不指定默认就是本机ADB。每次指令输入都要带指定服务器的指令前缀。
>
> 比如这些例子：
>
> adb -H [example.com](http://example.com) -P 5037 shell
>
> adb -H [example.com](http://example.com) -P 5037 logcat
>
> adb -H [example.com](http://example.com) -P 5037 install app.apk
>
> 如果不想每次都带，可以选择设置环境变量
>
> ADB_SERVER_SOCKET = “tcp:example.com:5037”
>
> 完事，这种就属于ADB的进阶使用了。想不到吧，其实ADB也能远程控制。
>
> 基本上只要知道ADB的运行原理之后就能做到更精细的和自由的自动化与控制，当然也别忘了注意网络安全。引言

>
> import socket
>
> import sys
>

>

>

>
> REMOTE_PORT = 5037
>
> async def pipe(reader, writer):
>
> try:
>
> while True:
>
> data = await reader.read(65536)
>

>
> break
>
> writer.write(data)
>
> await writer.drain()
>
> except (ConnectionResetError, BrokenPipeError, asyncio.CancelledError):
>
> pass

> finally:
>
> try:
>
> writer.close()
>
> await writer.wait_closed()
>
> except Exception:
>
> pass
>

>

>

>
> try:
>
> remote_reader, remote_writer = await asyncio.open_connection(REMOTE_ADDR, REMOTE_PORT)
>
> await asyncio.gather(
>
> pipe(client_reader, remote_writer),
>
> pipe(remote_reader, client_writer)
>
> )
>
> except Exception as e:
>
> print(f’[adb v6 proxy] error for {peer}: {e}')
>
> finally:
>
> if remote_writer:
>
> try:
>
> remote_writer.close()
>
> await remote_writer.wait_closed()
>
> except Exception:
>
> pass
>
> client_writer.close()
>
> try:
>
> await client_writer.wait_closed()
>
> except Exception:
>
> pass
>
> async def main():
>
> server = await asyncio.start_server(
>
> handle, LOCAL_ADDR, LOCAL_PORT,
>
> family=socket.AF_INET6,
>
> reuse_address=True
>
> )
>
> print(f’[adb v6 proxy] listening on [{LOCAL_ADDR}]:{LOCAL_PORT} → {REMOTE_ADDR}:{REMOTE_PORT}‘)
>
> print(’[adb v6 proxy] press Ctrl+C to stop’)
>
> async with server:
>
> await server.serve_forever()
>
> if name == ‘main’:
>
> try:
>
> asyncio.run(main())
>
> except KeyboardInterrupt:
>
> print(‘\n[adb v6 proxy] stopped’)
>
> sys.exit(0)
>
> （服务端运行这个脚本，将会自动转发流量到ADB服务器。当然如果你有ipv4公网就可以不用跑这个，这个是给ipv6用的。如果你的端口不是5037别忘了改脚本里的为你实际的端口）
>
> 最后别忘了防火墙的问题，要不然会被拦截：
>
> New-NetFirewallRule -Name “adb-v6” -DisplayName “adb-v6” -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 5037 -RemoteAddress Any -Action Allow
>
> 上面这个策略是允许所有IP通过，任何人只要扫到IP都能访问你的设备，还是不太安全。推荐指定放行来源IP段：
>
> New-NetFirewallRule -Name “adb-v6” -DisplayName “adb-v6” -Direction Inbound `
>
> -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 5037 -RemoteAddress 2409:xxxx::/64 -Action Allow
>
> 2409:xxxx::/64 为允许的来源IP(或IP段)，改成实际的你授权的那个人的就可以，减少暴露面，防止攻击。
>
> (依然是如果你的端口不是5037记得替换)
>
> 远程结束后用完后的清理
>
> 恢复防火墙策略
>
> netsh advfirewall firewall delete rule name=“adb-v6”
>
> 停止ADB服务器，所有客户机会被踢下线
>
> adb kill-server
>
> 如果你用了那个python转发器，直接关掉即可。同时记得在开发者选项里关无线调试和撤销ADB调试授权
>
> 客户机指令
>
> adb -H 有服务器的远程地址 -P 5037 devices
>
> 运行后会列出远程计算机上ADB连接的所有设备，5037是端口号。
>
> 其实本质上来说就是指定发送指令到的目标服务器而已，不指定默认就是本机ADB。每次指令输入都要带指定服务器的指令前缀。
>
> 比如这些例子：
>
> adb -H [example.com](http://example.com) -P 5037 shell
>
> adb -H [example.com](http://example.com) -P 5037 logcat
>
> adb -H [example.com](http://example.com) -P 5037 install app.apk
>
> 如果不想每次都带，可以选择设置环境变量
>
> ADB_SERVER_SOCKET = “tcp:example.com:5037”
>
> 完事，这种就属于ADB的进阶使用了。想不到吧，其实ADB也能远程控制。
>
> 基本上只要知道ADB的运行原理之后就能做到更精细的和自由的自动化与控制，当然也别忘了注意网络安全。

> 以下为项目介绍正文内容，AI生成、润色内容已使用截图方式发出
>
> ---
>
> 上链接：↓
>
> 仓库
>
> [mmaxou/IPProbe](https://github.com/mmaxou/IPProbe)
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/c/6/4/c64b0c6e5c3f45de71e693d92de898e82f32da4a_2_690x344.png)
> [GitHub - mmaxou/IPProbe: 本地IP探测+Bark推送+Cloudflare DDNS](https://github.com/mmaxou/IPProbe)
>
> 本地IP探测+Bark推送+Cloudflare DDNS
>
> ---
>
> 在公司用热点通过ipv6访问电脑的，就有了bark通知，然后离职了，为了一劳永逸，还是用赛博活佛的映射吧，就Vibe了一个rust版的类似ddns-go的桌面应用，UI异常简陋，主要实现如下功能：
>
>  本机IP地址探测（IPV4+IPV6，包含出口IP地址）
>
>  Bark程序通知，实现手机接收通知
>
>  CloudFlare DDNS 映射
>
>  开机自启、静默探测
>
>  较小的内存占用，软件9.56Mb，内存占用＜20Mb
>
> 注：后续不会进行更新，如有需要可自行二开或打包
>
> ---

### [Claude 11 月 12 日更新政策后的最新注册版](https://linux.do/t/topic/3193398)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-17 15:22 UTC · zh-CN · by qukang

> 看到claude code官方11月12号升级了策略反而激起了兴趣，于是尝试自己注册，把注册流程梳理了下。
>
> 先说下环境：
>
> Windows 电脑 → Ubuntu 虚拟机 → 独立住宅 IP → Claude→Google pay
>
> 没有直接用云主机是因为云主机还要钱，我直接再 Windows 上操作，开了一台 Ubuntu 虚拟机，给虚拟机配置了独立的住宅 IP，注册和后续操作都在 Ubuntu 里面完成。
>
> 主要是整套流程不算订阅费，才花了30，而且windows上的项目文件夹可以共享到虚拟机，这样cc可以读取使用。
>
> 比较意外的是，整个注册过程还挺顺利，没有触发 KFC，账号也正常注册成功了。
>
> 本来以为就这么结束了，没想到第二天账号直接被封了，这时候还没开始充值。
>
> 既然都折腾到这一步了，也不能就这么算了。于是写了一封英文申诉邮件找A/麻烦。
>
> 没想到当天上午提交申诉，下午账号就恢复了。
>
> 解封后我也没急着继续操作，先放了两天。
>
> 然后走了下 Google Pay 的付款，没想到这次非常顺利，一次就订阅成功。
>
> 从注册成功，到第二天封号，再到当天申诉解封，最后成功付款，整个过程还算顺利。
>
> 最近时间比较紧，先简单记录一下结果。后面有空再单独开个帖子，把 Ubuntu 虚拟机环境、网络配置、注册过程中遇到的问题、封号邮件和申诉过程，以及 Google Pay 付款的情况详细整理出来。
>
> 有些地方确实踩了不少坑，不过好在成本实在低，才30块钱。
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/c/2/3/c23a673e42f5e5cd31256caa92cd13ae92ae5f67_2_690x440.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/c/2/3/c23a673e42f5e5cd31256caa92cd13ae92ae5f67.png)

### [免费一级域名一年](https://linux.do/t/topic/3193251)

`linuxdo:福利羊毛` · T2 · 2026-11-17 14:55 UTC · zh-CN · by DreamKing

> [![IMG_0377](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/a/8/1/a81fed5f0d36a0e08922190ca298bdcdc1f1e292_2_690x485.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/a/8/1/a81fed5f0d36a0e08922190ca298bdcdc1f1e292.jpeg)
>
> https://gravatar.com   免费一级域名一年
>
> 官方支持的后缀是 .bio、.fyi、.life、.ninja、.rocks、.contact、.guru、.link、.place、.social、.cool、.info、.live、.pro、.world
>
> 只免首年，不是永久免费。
>
> Gravatar 本身是 Automattic 的头像 / 个人资料服务，这个域名是用来做你的 Gravatar 资料地址的，不是通用域名。官网写的是：选域名、首年免费、一键设置，支持页也写着目前所有域名首年免费，续费细节在结账时显示。
>
> 一个资料只能有 1 个自定义域名**，也不能接入已在别处注册的域名。
>
> 免费域名没有 DNS 管理，就是说它只能指向你的 Gravatar 资料页，不能像普通域名那样自由解析、建站。想转出倒是可以，官网说随时能转到别的注册商。

### [colima/Docker 容器内如何让容器内所有网络流量透明地走 SOCKS5 代理](https://linux.do/t/topic/3193034)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-17 14:13 UTC · zh-CN · by dddd

> 目前在 macOS 上进行开发，使用 Colima 启动 Docker
>
> 由于网络环境的限制，Mac 默认只能访问少量白名单网络出口，大部分外部网络请求无法直接连接。
>
> 不过，提供了一个官方允许使用的 SOCKS5/HTTPS 代理出口，可以通过该代理访问其他网络资源。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24896922-h-1我想实现的效果
>
> 希望 Docker 容器内的所有出站网络流量，都能在网络层自动通过指定的 SOCKS5 代理（或者 HTTPS 代理）转发，而不需要在每个容器或应用程序里单独配置代理。
>
> 详细点就是：
>
> 全局透明代理：无论容器内运行的是 curl、git、apt、pip、npm，还是其他自定义程序，都能自动通过代理访问外部网络。
>
> 不依赖应用层代理配置：不希望通过设置 HTTP_PROXY、HTTPS_PROXY、ALL_PROXY 等环境变量来实现，因为部分程序不支持这些变量。
>
> DNS 请求也能正确处理：希望避免出现代理已配置，但 DNS 解析仍然走默认网络出口的问题。
>
> 想问下大佬有没有这方面的研究或者实践

### [从Anthropic的招股书看，deepseek放弃C端free用户完全正确](https://linux.do/t/topic/3192943)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-17 13:56 UTC · zh-CN · by gobert

> ANT的算力60%用于训练，40%用于推理，而且ANT的卡还普遍是B200/B300，也就是说即便是强如claude,也是要留出大部分算力用于训练，只有小部分用于推理服务，而且claude的推理服务重点还是放在API用户，订阅用户分到的比重要远少于api用户
>
> deepseek没有ANT这么多算力，估计连ANT1/10都不一定有，如果要把重心放在训练上，这意味着他要拿出更高比例的算力来放在训练上，claude是60%，deepseek可能需要70%80%甚至100%，也就是完全放弃免费C端用户是非常值得的，完全放弃付费API用户也是值得的，因为训练出SOTA模型的商业回报、股市回报要远远高于这点订阅或者api的费用
>
> 在算力有限的情况下，现在放弃放弃C端free用户完全正确，未来放弃B端/C端 api用户也没有问题，都是基模厂发展的合理且正确的策略

> 试了很多临时 root 工具，最后都要放弃了，都准备直接解 BL 直接开干了，最后抱着侥幸的心态下载了 DirtyFrag，结果 3 秒成功![:distorted_face:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/distorted_face.png?v=16)
>
> [![1000022007.jpg](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/1/0/f/10fbc814223d59a0bfee95aa0dfb063b7ae8c7d7_2_226x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/1/0/f/10fbc814223d59a0bfee95aa0dfb063b7ae8c7d7.jpeg)
>
> 当时还没反应过来，我愣在原地缓了一会，才接受了我临时 root 成功的事实（人生中的第一个 root）
>
> 我恍恍惚惚的不知道要干嘛，网上搜了一下 LSPosed，给微信、QQ 打上防撤回，简化一下一些垃圾软件
>
> 于是我下载了这些模块
>
> [![1000022115.jpg](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/c/2/6/c26d81abc0a2ccb4bd3f67d846a947165240d749_2_389x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/c/2/6/c26d81abc0a2ccb4bd3f67d846a947165240d749.jpeg)
>
> 安装模块的时候，右下角有个大大的重启按钮，它是硬重启。重启之后临时 root 会掉，不要点右下角的重启按钮，而是退回到主页，然后点击右上角选择软重启，这样临时 root 不掉，而模块也能正常应用更改。
>
> 事实上，掉临时 root 倒没什么，大不了重新再花 3 秒 root 一下就行了，但我发现它好像是靠运气的，硬重启后 我尝试重新获取临时 root，一直失败，但多试几次又能成功，失败的画面是这样的
>
> ![:distorted_face:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/distorted_face.png?v=16)
>
> [![1000022059.jpg](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/d/9/5/d9536af4e313c092dc06bf757066361da16166aa_2_226x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/d/9/5/d9536af4e313c092dc06bf757066361da16166aa.jpeg)
>
> 软重启 不要硬重启！
>
> Vector 模块是 Lsposed，需要安装 Zygisk，问了 AI 他推荐我用 ReZygisk，对顺序好像有要求的，如果不按顺序走，就比如下面这样，不知道为什么会冒红，先安装 zygisk 再安装 vector 就可以了
>
> [![1000022072.jpg](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/3/d/3/3d33377fe83877eb978064791de0890fb097830d_2_226x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/3/d/3/3d33377fe83877eb978064791de0890fb097830d.jpeg)
>
> 接下来就是我安装的一些 LSPosed 的模块
>
> [![1000022116.jpg](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/1/f/f/1ff4d2572125e2874ffab96011655debe3e81c90_2_225x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/1/f/f/1ff4d2572125e2874ffab96011655debe3e81c90.jpeg)
>
> 关于微信防撤回 我最开始安装的是 FkWeChat，因为它开源免费，但是不知道为什么，它的防撤回功能无效，但是它其他功能可以使用。那就违背初心用回商业的 WXEntry）
>
> 底部液态玻璃那个模块的效果就如下图所示
>
> [![1000022119.jpg](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/a/5/a/a5ad88b4e3292bc30b2cb30b702999f333df6975_2_226x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/a/5/a/a5ad88b4e3292bc30b2cb30b702999f333df6975.jpeg)
>
> （我是分隔符）
>
> [![1000022117.jpg](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/9/f/a/9fadae65a6e67c0f03c3714909adda1e69a8df17_2_226x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/9/f/a/9fadae65a6e67c0f03c3714909adda1e69a8df17.jpeg)
>
> 微信那有点幽默了，底下那个卡得不上不下的![:sweat_smile:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/sweat_smile.png?v=16)
>
> 我感觉比较难绷的是那个缺德地图变成高德地图了，简洁得我有点害怕![:fearful:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/fearful.png?v=16)
>
> [![1000022121.jpg](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/d/8/3/d8301f0816696e1f53b0e044ba717cfcac277ce7_2_226x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/d/8/3/d8301f0816696e1f53b0e044ba717cfcac277ce7.jpeg)
>
> 还有朋友去推荐我搞 VCAM（虚拟摄像头）和微信 Agent 模块
>
> 不过我没需求就不搞了
>
> 其实我最想搞的是破解步道乐跑，实现坐地日行八万里![:laughing:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/laughing.png?v=16)
>

>
> ---
>
> [!NOTE] 「纪尧姆·阿波利奈尔」是谁？
>
> [![1dq8P5kT8JGMZRE3gt0Z2nE5F2tiOtcnmKJAubYe40hSVW657Sj5NpfzTRrUiCpiFSla7vaZ1gRCBf3CwrDQzfASYvfuW66XPZoVKeKD8vwChioaIDst5CfkkXXKpNdcKg0Llv0CI4ABZ7vVeIFMl9Lz1uBhI_Sjgyua1sEkeeqOiY07lipC0uzUxo5aAY_y](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/b/f/e/bfe62ce89c5805cef52d91b311cb148f9873ec60_2_339x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/b/f/e/bfe62ce89c5805cef52d91b311cb148f9873ec60.jpeg)
>
> 纪尧姆·阿波利奈尔原名威廉·阿尔贝·弗沃兹米日·阿波利纳里·科斯特罗维茨基，1880年8月26日出生于罗马。他的母亲是一位性格桀骜、常年出入赌场的波兰没落贵族女子，生父据传为意大利军官兼教廷贵族。这种私生子的隐秘身世与跨国漂泊的成长轨迹，赋予了他天生的波希米亚气质与文化杂糅感。少年时期他在摩纳哥、戛纳与尼斯求学，1899年随家人迁居巴黎。尽管早期做过银行职员与家庭教师，阿波利奈尔很快便凭借过人的文学才华、渊博的秘学知识与极具感染力的个人魅力，成为20世纪初巴黎蒙马特“洗濯船”（Bateau-Lavoir）与蒙帕纳斯前卫艺术圈无可争议的精神枢纽。他与毕加索、勃拉克的友谊催生了立体主义的理论自觉，是他发掘并向世人盛赞了“关税员”亨利·卢梭的纯真艺术，他与女画家玛丽·洛朗桑那段跌宕起伏的恋情更化作了法兰西现代诗歌史上最动人的抒情绝唱。1911年卢浮宫《蒙娜丽莎》失窃案发后，他因早年曾收留过盗取卢浮宫伊比利亚雕像的前秘书而受牵连，被警方短暂关押于桑特监狱六天，这段荒诞而屈辱的铁窗经历不仅震撼了整个巴黎文坛，也直接融入了他日后的诗篇。
>
> 1914年第一次世界大战爆发后，原本没有法国国籍的阿波利奈尔主动申请入籍并报名从军，先后在炮兵与步兵部队服役。在泥泞血腥的战壕中，他甚至依然保持着高昂的创作激情，在炮火间隙用钢笔在桦树皮与战地明信片上写诗。1916年3月17日，他在战壕中低头阅读《法兰西信使》杂志时，被一枚德军炮弹的弹片击穿钢盔、嵌入右太阳穴。历经惊险的颅骨钻孔手术后，他虽奇迹般幸存，性格与体质却受到重创；毕加索等人为他绘制的头缠厚重绷带的侧面肖像，成为现代主义一代在工业战争机器碾压下的悲剧图腾。1918年11月9日，即一战停战协定签署前两天，身体虚弱的阿波利奈尔因感染席卷全球的西班牙大流感在巴黎寓所病逝，年仅38岁。当他咽下最后一口气时，窗外欢庆胜利的巴黎民众正高呼着“打倒威廉（Guillaume）！”——人们诅咒的是德皇威廉二世，却在历史残酷的巧合中成了这位同名诗人的送葬挽歌。
>
> 阿波利奈尔的思想与美学贡献，首先体现在他是现代视觉艺术革命最具远见的“立法者”。在1913年出版的评论集《立体派画家：美学沉思》（Les Peintres cubistes）中，他首次系统地为毕加索、勃拉克、格里斯等人的艺术实验建立理论框架。他指出，传统绘画受制于文艺复兴以来的单点透视与视觉摹仿，而立体主义则是一场追求“概念真实”而非“视觉真实”的哲学革命，它试图在平面上引入非欧几何与第四维度（时间与精神的维度）。在此书中，他还专门创立了奥尔甫斯主义（Orphism）这一概念，用以概括罗伯特·德劳内、费尔南·莱热等人将纯粹色彩对比、光线律动与音乐抽象性融为一体的全新创作倾向，直接预示了西方纯抽象艺术的诞生。
>
> 在诗歌领域，阿波利奈尔同样发动了一场彻底的语言与形式革命。1913年出版的诗集《醇酒集》（Alcools）是20世纪现代诗歌的分水岭。在交付印刷的最后校样阶段，阿波利奈尔做出了一个惊世骇俗的决定——删去全书所有的标点符号。他认为，标点符号不过是外部强加给语言的机械拐杖，真正的诗歌应当完全依靠自身内在的呼吸节奏、语音回响与意象跃迁来实现断句与流转。在开篇长诗 《地带》（Zone）中，他将立体主义的 共时性（Simultaneity） 原则引入诗歌：埃菲尔铁塔化作看管桥群羊群的牧羊女，呼啸的飞机与神话中的凤凰、伊卡洛斯同框翱翔，街头招贴广告、工厂车间、移民潮与天主教的流血圣心毫无等级地并置交织，展现出工业现代性既令人眩晕又饱含乡愁的宏大景观；而在名篇《米拉波桥》（Le Pont Mirabeau）中，塞纳河水的奔流与爱恋的消逝在无标点的吟唱中达成了古典悲剧般的永恒。到了1918年出版的《图画诗集》（Calligrammes）中，他更进一步将诗歌从听觉的线性时间解放至视觉的二维空间，把诗句排印成斜落的雨丝、跃动的骏马、被刺穿的心脏、领带、怀表乃至埃菲尔铁塔的具象图形，开创了现代具象诗（Concrete Poetry）与视觉排版艺术的先河。
>
> 更为深远的是，阿波利奈尔是人类思想史上超现实主义（surréalisme）一词的真正缔造者。1917年春天，他在为芭蕾舞剧《游行》撰写的节目单以及荒诞戏剧《蒂蕾西亚的乳房》（Les Mamelles de Tirésias）的序言中，正式铸造了这一词汇。他在序言中以一个精妙的哲学比喻阐释道：当人类想要模仿“行走”这一动作时，发明出来的并不是带有双腿的机械假人，而是形状与腿毫无相似之处、却能实现高速移动的“车轮”——这便是艺术上的“超现实主义”。在他看来，艺术家绝不应做自然表象的奴隶式抄写员，而应通过想象力的自由重组创造出比现实本身更切中本质的“新实在”。在他辞世前夕发表的纲领性演讲 《新精神与诗人》（1917）中，他将惊奇（la surprise）确立为现代艺术最核心的发条，号召诗人走出象牙塔，大胆拥抱电影、留声机、电报与航空技术。阿波利奈尔如同一座横跨世纪的灯塔，将19世纪波德莱尔、兰波的象征主义遗产，成功摆渡到了达达主义与超现实主义的新大陆。

> 佬们我有个问题，比如说我在使用3588进行算力优化，发现当前的算力瓶颈卡在了NPU侧，但是RKNN编译器不公开导致无法再往下继续进行算力优化，而使用香橙派AIPro就能在遇到NPU侧的瓶颈时进行进行NPU侧的算子算力优化。
>
> 那既然普通的开发者使用3588进行算力优化触及不到NPU这个核心领域，那在应聘3588端侧算力优化的方向时我们的核心竞争力应该是什么呢？还是说想要体验完整的CPU+NPU侧的算力优化流程还是使用香橙派AIPro比较好 ![:thinking:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/thinking.png?v=16)
>
> 如果后面想要继续使用3588作为算力平台进行算力优化的话，是不是应该找一个是在固定场景下的开源项目来定位主要耗时，在此基础上作为自己的项目，但是现在找不到这样固定场景的开源项目 ![:thinking:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/thinking.png?v=16)

> 最近在做两个项目，非常缺token。我原本在用的claude号是年初开的一直用到现在，没有kyc的情况下开过两次pro，上个月再次订阅的时候弹kyc了，用护照验证后用了三个礼拜。在一个美好的清晨，弹了portal kyc，尝试邪修未果，最后还是用护照验了，然后秒封。看很多佬友申诉后解封，但是我申诉完没过多久就被狠狠拒绝了 ![:sob:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/sob.png?v=16)

### [五险一金的正确打开方式](https://linux.do/t/topic/3192562)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-17 12:39 UTC · zh-CN · by DevExzh

> 看到有不少佬友觉得五险一金是按照工资算的，其实对也不对 ![:distorted_face:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/distorted_face.png?v=16)
>
> 险种
> 单位承担比例公司
> 个人承担比例
> 说明
>
> 养老保险
> 16%
> 8%
> 个人部分全部计入个人账户
>
> 医疗保险
> 约 8%（部分地区含生育合并）
> 2%
> 部分地区个人每月另需交几元大病统筹
>
> 失业保险
> 0.5%
> 0.5%
> 城镇/农村户籍部分地区略有差异
>
> 工伤保险
> 0.3% - 0.6%（按行业浮动）
> 0%
> 个人不缴费，由单位承担
>
> 生育保险
> 0.4% - 1%（部分与医保合并）
> 0%
> 个人不缴费，由单位承担
>
> 公积金是个人和单位各自承担 5~12%
>
> 那么应该怎么算呢？
>
> 拿税前工资先算一下缴费基数，它是有区间的：
>
> 最低：社平工资的 60%
>
> 最高：社平工资 3 倍
>
> 如果税前工资低于最低基数，就按照最低基数缴；高于最高基数就按照最高基数缴。社平工资是跟你劳动合同所在地相关联的，一线城市大概就是 1w 左右
>
> 举几个例子，假设月薪 4k，那么基数就是 1w x 0.6 = 6k，要按照 6k 去缴五险一金；月薪 4w，超过了 1w x 3，所以只能按照 3w 缴。
>
> 实际到手工资是按照 你税前工资 - 五险一金 - 个人所得税 算的。个税是阶梯计税方式，按照档次计税，具体计算方式可以看各地税局的个税计算器。
>
> 简单来说就是，你的税前工资 - 起征点 - 速算扣除数 - (可能的附加扣除)，按照 3%、10%、20%、 …… 依次计税
>
> 3% 对应区间内的收入按照 3% 税率计税，超过 3% 的部分以 10% 计税，以此类推
>
> 然后每个人每年还可以有一次性的收入，比如年终奖什么的，它是按照你具体收入定档计税的，比如说你对应的档是 10%，那就是整个年终奖按照 10% 计税，不是工资收入阶梯计税
>
> 如果收入高到一定程度，大概的收入构成就可以是：
>
> 月度工资一部分
>
> 年终奖一部分
>
> 大头走分红，因为分红只需要 20% 的个税，而全走工资形式是最多能到 45% 的，很不划算，到手砍半
>
> 如果有遗漏，佬友也可以补充下

### [浅谈web_search工具](https://linux.do/t/topic/3192518)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-17 12:29 UTC · zh-CN · by √33

> 在使用 agent 的过程中，联网扩展是一个很重要的内容。 本文不考虑 tool_choice 参数，只是帮助小白大致理解各种 agent 的 web_search 能力的实现，可能存在部分错误
>
> https://linux.do#p-24893428-h-1场景模拟
>
> Cli：ClaudeCode
>
> Model：DeepSeek 官 /deepseek
>
> https://linux.do#p-24893428-tools-2Tools 分类（工具调用)
>
> 根据 tool_call 过程是否在本地执行，粗略的将 tool 分为两种
>
> 本地 tool，如 edit、read，grep 等。 表现为，当模型返回 tool_call 时，本地执行对应 tool, 也包括调用 Remote MCP，然后将执行结果返回给 deepseek，最终模型结合执行结果输出文本。在发送请求是，tool 的类型（type）常见为 function、custom
>
> 服务端 Tool，此类工具对用户来说几乎是透明的，tool_call 过程是在服务端完成的，模型会返回最终的结果 + 部分过程内容（如查询的网址的列表、标题、链接)。在发送请求时，有属于自己的 type。
>
> 以使用 web_search 查询本周 github 热点项目为例： 本地工具调用如下图所示：
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/f/c/0/fc083d4b5bbb3975799acd868aaeb319ec7ed40c_2_689x430.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/f/c/0/fc083d4b5bbb3975799acd868aaeb319ec7ed40c.png)
>
> 服务端 tool 如下图所示：
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/6/3/a/63a1e7bbdfccb969e7846004cb0177aca799eb4b_2_690x458.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/6/3/a/63a1e7bbdfccb969e7846004cb0177aca799eb4b.png)
>
> 可以直白的看出，服务端 tool 就直接在厂商那里帮你干完活，返回了最终结果
>
> https://linux.do#p-24893428-web_search-3关于 web_search
>
> https://linux.do#p-24893428-web_search-4服务端 web_search
>
> 回到 api 文档，在文档中 web_search 是不同于普通的 tool，是单独列出来的， 下图截取自 claude api 文档
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/8/7/4/874fdc69f9b833b40f8b3fccebd6fb4b8ce20062_2_490x500.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/8/7/4/874fdc69f9b833b40f8b3fccebd6fb4b8ce20062.png)
>
> OpenAI、DeepSeek 中，web_search 也作为一种不同于普通的 tool 类型单独列出。
>
> 大胆猜想一下，如果在 API 请求的 tools 中包含 web_search，告诉厂商，启用了该功能，如果厂商支持 web_search，并且模型也选择了使用厂商自带的 web_search，那么这次调用就会在厂商的服务端执行，这下就知道为什么 web_search 工具调用收费了吧。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24893428-mcp-5插件、MCP 扩展
>
> 常见的有 exa-mcp 、perplexity-mcp、浏览器插件扩展，以及各 agent 的 web 插件。

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-17 12:14 UTC · zh-CN · by StoneHeart

### [分享一套工程思考用的Prompt，大伙有没有存货交换下](https://linux.do/t/topic/3192392)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-17 12:00 UTC · zh-CN · by 鲨鱼辣椒

> 最近两个月一直在用 Agent 做开发运维，沉淀了几条高频在用、非常受用的 Prompt，抛砖引玉，也想看看大家有没有私藏好用的，一起交流：
>
> 从第一性原理出发，找到最本质原因，修复一下。
>
> 先问一些不清晰的问题，对齐我的喜好，然后再出3版方案。
>
> 不要默认我提出的问题定义就是正确的。你先分析我真正想解决的底层需求，判断我有没有把症状误认为原因、把手段误认为目标。如果存在更值得解决的问题，直接指出来。
>
> 不要只考虑这个改动产生的直接效果。继续推演它的二阶、三阶影响，尤其关注对其他模块、用户行为、系统复杂度和长期维护成本的潜在影响。
>
> 其他领域里有没有类似的方案，用跨领域的方式全面思考，找到最优解。
>
> 先假设你当前认为最合理的方案是错误的。站在最强反对者的角度，寻找能够推翻它的证据、反例和边界情况。然后重新评估方案，看看有没有更好的解法。
>
> 深入分析整个代码库的 Git 历史、关键 PR 和架构演变过程。找出哪些设计是有意为之，哪些是历史遗留，哪些是为了解决已经不存在的问题而引入的。识别可以安全移除的历史包袱。
>
> 假设明天有一个完全不了解项目、但是能力很强的工程师来接手。请评估他理解整个项目需要付出的认知成本，找出那些命名混乱、抽象过度、职责不清晰、需要大量上下文才能理解的代码，并提出简化方案。
>
> 全面分析最近XX天里的所有的PR，找出最慢的那几个，看看有没有导致卡顿、可以优化的地方。
>
> 全面复盘最近XX时间的 Bug、返工、回滚和重复修改。不要只统计发生了什么，要分析这些问题背后有没有共同的根因。把能够预防的共性问题沉淀成项目规则、自动化或者 Skill，避免我们反复支付同样的成本。
>
> ---
>
> 转自卡兹克
>
> 各位有没有自己日常喂给 Agent 的优质 Prompt？欢迎分享。
